item.title: Episode 53: A universal flu shot aims at the neuraminidase
item.description: Rationally designed hyperglycosylated neuraminidase (NA) immunogen elicits broad, cross-subtype anti-NA humoral responses (Hecht, Nait Mohamed, Zhang, Rawson, Lee, Murphy, Thornlow Lamson, Ronsard, Caradonna, Lingwood, Schmidt; Ragon Institute of MGH/MIT/Harvard; bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.08.08.743685, posted 2026-08-14, abstract-only pending full-text rendering): iterative hyperglycosylation of variable NA epitopes preserves enzymatic activity and antibody reactivity at the conserved catalytic site; in mice the hyperglycosylated immunogen produced serum antibody titers comparable to wild-type NA but with markedly increased breadth — recognition of N2 NAs from H2N2 and H3N2 strains spanning nearly 65 years of antigenic drift plus heterosubtypic recognition of an N9 NA; single B-cell isolation yielded a monoclonal antibody targeting a previously undefined conserved epitope at the NA tetramer interface, and passive transfer of that antibody partially protected mice against lethal heterologous influenza challenge — a clean proof-of-concept that glycan shielding can steer humoral responses toward the deeply conserved, catalytic-site-adjacent surface that a universal NA-based flu vaccine would need to engage, relevant to the H5N1 stockpile-strategy discussion. HUTCHMED and AstraZeneca announce positive topline SAFFRON Phase 3 readout for ORPATHYS (savolitinib) plus TAGRISSO (osimertinib) vs platinum-doublet chemotherapy in EGFR-mutated, MET-driven advanced NSCLC after progression on osimertinib (BioSpace/GlobeNewswire press release, 2026-08-17): 338-patient randomized global trial across 230 centers in 29 countries; prospectively enrolled MET-high tumors using IHC+FISH cutoffs derived from the earlier SAVANNAH Phase 2 dataset; savolitinib 300 mg BID + osimertinib 80 mg QD hit both co-primary endpoints, statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in PFS and OS with no new safety findings; specific HRs/medians undisclosed pending medical-meeting presentation; savolitinib is an oral selective MET tyrosine kinase inhibitor already approved in China (SACHI Phase 3) and temporarily authorized in Switzerland; SAFFRON forms the basis for global regulatory submissions and would establish the first oral doublet designed for MET-driven post-osimertinib resistance — ~1 in 3 progressing EGFR+ NSCLC patients — and make MET testing at progression a standard-of-care question. BioKinema: physically grounded generative model produces continuous-time all-atom biomolecular trajectories at a fraction of classical MD cost (Feng, Zhang, Zhang, Cao, Zhang, Barth, Liu, Li; primarily EPFL; bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.02.15.705956v2, posted 2026-08-15, abstract-only): spatial-temporal diffusion architecture motivated by exponential decay of correlations under Langevin dynamics, explicitly trained to reproduce correct kinetics and thermodynamics, with a hierarchical forecasting-and-interpolation strategy to control long-horizon drift; reproduces equilibrium free-energy landscape and conformational kinetics for protein systems, captures ligand-driven conformational changes and allosteric effects in protein–ligand complexes, and predicts rare kinetic events including ligand unbinding pathways when supplied with enhanced-sampling data — direction-of-travel evidence that deep-learning surrogates are moving from static structure to dynamics prediction, with implications for cryptic-pocket detection, allosteric drug design, and residence-time prediction. Haplodiploidy does NOT independently favor eusocial evolution across insects (Suresh, Linksvayer; Arizona State University; Current Biology vol 36 issue 15, doi:10.1016/j.cub.2026.06.041; news coverage ScienceDaily/phys.org 2026-08-13): phylogenetic comparative analysis across ~69,000 insect species on two species-level trees tests the 1960s W.D. Hamilton hypothesis that haplodiploid relatedness asymmetries (full sisters share ~3/4 of genes vs 1/2 with own daughters) primed Hymenoptera for eusociality; on first pass the association is present, but essentially the entire signal traces to a single clade — the aculeate Hymenoptera (stinging ants, bees, wasps) — and once that lineage is accounted for, haplodiploid and diploid insects evolve eusociality at comparable rates; the beautiful sixty-year-old kin-selection story doesn't survive at insect-wide scale, and authors propose lineage-specific traits (stingers, mass provisioning, controlled nesting) as the more plausible drivers.
item.itunes:summary: Rationally designed hyperglycosylated neuraminidase immunogen elicits broad cross-subtype anti-NA antibodies in mice (Hecht, Nait Mohamed, Schmidt et al.; Ragon Institute; bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.08.08.743685, 2026-08-14, abstract-only): iterative extra-glycan shielding of variable NA epitopes preserves enzymatic activity and catalytic-site antigenicity; hyperglycosylated immunogen produced comparable serum titers to wild-type NA but with breadth spanning ~65 years of N2 antigenic drift plus heterosubtypic N9 recognition; single-B-cell isolation of a monoclonal against a previously undefined conserved NA tetramer-interface epitope that partially protected mice on passive transfer — a clean glycan-shielding proof-of-concept for a universal NA-based flu vaccine, relevant to the H5N1 stockpile-strategy conversation. HUTCHMED and AstraZeneca announce positive SAFFRON Phase 3 readout (BioSpace/GlobeNewswire 2026-08-17): ORPATHYS (savolitinib, oral selective MET tyrosine kinase inhibitor) plus TAGRISSO (osimertinib) vs platinum-doublet chemotherapy in 338 patients across 230 centers/29 countries with EGFR-mutated MET-amplified/-overexpressed NSCLC after progression on osimertinib; hit both co-primary endpoints with statistically significant and clinically meaningful PFS and OS improvement, safety consistent with each drug alone, specific HRs and medians undisclosed pending medical meeting; MET amplification/overexpression is the driver in ~1 in 3 post-osimertinib progressions and this would be the first oral doublet targeting it, making MET testing at progression a standard-of-care question. BioKinema: physically grounded generative model for all-atom biomolecular trajectories (Feng, Barth et al.; EPFL; bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.02.15.705956v2, 2026-08-15, abstract-only): spatial-temporal diffusion architecture motivated by the exponential decay of correlations under Langevin dynamics, hierarchical forecasting-and-interpolation to control long-horizon drift, and explicit training to reproduce correct kinetics and thermodynamics; reproduces equilibrium free-energy landscapes and conformational kinetics, captures ligand-driven conformational changes and allosteric effects in protein–ligand complexes, and predicts rare kinetic events like ligand unbinding pathways — a serious entry in the shift from static structure prediction to dynamics prediction, with implications for cryptic-pocket detection, allosteric drug design, and residence-time prediction. Haplodiploidy does not independently favor eusocial evolution across insects (Suresh, Linksvayer; Arizona State University; Current Biology vol 36 issue 15, doi:10.1016/j.cub.2026.06.041; news 2026-08-13): phylogenetic comparative analysis on ~69,000 insect species on two large trees tests the 1960s Hamilton kin-selection hypothesis that haplodiploid relatedness asymmetries primed ants, bees, and wasps for eusociality; the pattern is real but almost entirely driven by a single clade (aculeate Hymenoptera), and once controlled for, haplodiploid and diploid insects evolve eusociality at comparable rates — the sixty-year-old textbook story doesn't survive at insect-wide scale; lineage-specific traits (stingers, mass provisioning, nesting) are proposed as the more plausible drivers.

item.title: Episode 52: DRC's Ebola outbreak becomes the largest on record
item.description: WHO Disease Outbreak News update on Bundibugyo virus disease in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (WHO DON615, published 2026-08-14): as of 12 August 2026 the outbreak has reached 4,686 cumulative confirmed cases and 2,186 deaths (crude CFR 46.8%), with 4,665 cases/2,184 deaths in DRC, 20 cases/2 deaths in Uganda, and imported cases in France and Germany; declared a PHEIC on 17 May 2026 and now the largest Ebola outbreak ever reported in DRC, having expanded from Mongbwalu (Ituri) to 54 health zones across 6 provinces (Ituri accounts for 85% of cases); peak weekly incidence was 579 cases and 304 deaths in epi-week 32 (3–9 August); the etiological agent is Bundibugyo ebolavirus (BDBV) — a genetically distinct ebolavirus first identified in western Uganda in 2007 that has historically caused smaller outbreaks with CFR 25–40% and never before an event of this scale; the licensed Ervebo vaccine is designed against Zaire ebolavirus glycoprotein (GP), which differs from Bundibugyo GP by ~40% at the amino-acid level with distinct immunodominant epitopes — making cross-protection a live scientific question the current DRC vaccine and PARTNERS monoclonal-antibody trials (100+ patients enrolled since 2 July across 3 Ituri facilities) are being run to answer. Definium Therapeutics (Nasdaq: DFTX) reports positive topline Phase 3 Voyage results for DT120 ODT (lysergide, LSD) in generalized anxiety disorder (BusinessWire/BioSpace press release + HCPLive + Psychiatric Times, 2026-08-12): 214-patient randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study across ~35 U.S. sites (n=107 per arm, baseline HAM-A ~27–28) of a single 100 μg dose of a lysergide orally disintegrating tablet vs placebo with primary endpoint change in HAM-A at week 12; DT120 delivered a placebo-adjusted HAM-A reduction of 5.4 points (LSM change −11.6 vs −6.2 placebo; p<0.0001; Cohen's d=0.81, a “large” effect vs the ~0.3 typical of SSRIs); responder rate (≥50% HAM-A reduction) 43% vs 16% placebo; remission (HAM-A ≤7) 14% vs 4%; safety clean — TEAEs mild-to-moderate, transient, largely confined to dosing day, no suicidality signal; DT120 is a 5-HT2A partial agonist with the therapeutic hypothesis grounded in sustained neuroplasticity/synaptogenesis following a single dosing session; the first plausibly approvable classical-psychedelic medicine on a clean Phase 3 pivotal readout; confirmatory Phase 3 (Panorama, includes 50 μg arm) reads out September 2026 and, if positive, would restart the psychedelic-medicine regulatory arc after the 2024 Lykos MDMA CRL. AI4Loop: deep-learning framework infers gene-centered 3D chromatin interaction networks from RNA-seq alone across 12,347 tumor transcriptomes / 32 cancer types and flags oxazolidinone antibiotics as chromatin-loop reversers (Dao, Lebeau, Amuley, Tan, Li, Goh, Chng, Kwoh, Lin, Lyu, Fullwood; National University of Singapore / Cancer Science Institute; bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.08.12.744314, posted 2026-08-14, abstract-only pending full-text rendering): interaction networks recovered from RNA-seq alone match orthogonal Hi-C datasets across cell types, outperform gene expression at cancer classification, and reveal pervasive increases in gene-centered chromatin interactions at oncogene-associated loci as a pan-cancer feature; integration with >50,000 drug-treated transcriptomes prospectively identified eperezolid and radezolid (oxazolidinone antibiotics, linezolid class) as chromatin-gain reversers, confirmed by Hi-C in breast cancer cells — a computational-to-experimental drug-repurposing pipeline that generated a genuinely non-obvious hit; plausible mechanisms include mitochondrial-protein-synthesis inhibition feeding into metabolite-driven chromatin regulation (e.g., α-ketoglutarate) or an uncharacterized off-target eukaryotic effect. Alibaba releases Qwen3.8-27B open-weight model (Apache 2.0, 2026-08-14): 27.78B-parameter hybrid decoder (64 layers: 48 gated DeltaNet linear-attention + 16 full-attention, GQA), 262K native context extensible to 1M via YaRN, multimodal (text/image/video); reported benchmarks: SWE-bench Pro 61.7 (vs Opus 4.8 53.4), LiveCodeBench v6 90.3 (vs 88.8), OSWorld-Verified 84.3 (vs 72.7), AndroidWorld 81.9 (vs 62.0); Opus still leads on GPQA Diamond (89.2 vs 92.0) and Terminal-Bench 2.1 (73.0 vs 78.9); fits on a single 24GB consumer GPU when Q4-quantized (~17GB weights), which brings frontier-adjacent agentic coding to on-prem/local deployments — relevant to any biomedical workflow with data that can't leave a locked-down environment. Sexual somersault behavior in redback spiders (Latrodectus hasselti) is controlled by X-chromosome-linked genetic module(s) distinct from abdominal-constriction escape (Uludağ, University of Hamburg; Biology Letters, 2026-08-12, doi:10.1098/rsbl.2026.0211): 104 hybrid matings filmed by IR camera between redbacks (which somersault into the female's fangs during copulation and are cannibalized) and katipō (Latrodectus katipo, no somersault, diverged ~100 kya) show both traits inherit via the X chromosome but do NOT co-segregate — ~50% of hybrids performed one behavior without the other — implying the somersault and the escape maneuver are separately-inheritable modules with loci “very far apart on the same chromosome or on different chromosomes.”

item.title: Episode 51: Bristol's molecular glue arrives for myeloma
item.description: Protective effect of A(H5N8) stockpiled vaccine against a virus genetically identical to a human isolate of bovine A(H5N1) influenza virus (Uraki, Kiso, Iwatsuki-Horimoto, Ito, Yamayoshi, Imai, Kawaoka; University of Tokyo Pandemic Preparedness Center + University of Wisconsin-Madison Veterinary Medicine; eBioMedicine vol 131, published 2026-08-11, doi:10.1016/j.ebiom.2026.106430): first direct in vivo test of whether a pre-pandemic H5 stockpile actually protects against the U.S. bovine H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b now circulating in dairy cattle; the AS03-adjuvanted inactivated Japanese stockpile is based on the H5N8 strain A/Astrakhan/3212/2020 (same clade 2.3.4.4b, different neuraminidase); mice and ferrets vaccinated and then challenged with a virus genetically identical to a human isolate of bovine A(H5N1) mounted robust neutralizing antibody responses, showed significantly suppressed viral replication in organs, and had complete protection against lethal challenge, while all unvaccinated animals died — demonstrates strong cross-protective efficacy across neuraminidase subtypes and validates the pre-pandemic stockpile strategy for the specific bovine A(H5N1) contingency that most concerns public-health authorities now; the field can worry less about needing an exact H–N match for a stockpiled shot; caveats are dose-finding/durability in humans and future drift within clade 2.3.4.4b. FDA grants accelerated approval to Bristol Myers Squibb's ZENBEXUS (iberdomide) plus daratumumab/hyaluronidase-fihj and dexamethasone (ZDd) for multiple myeloma patients after ≥1 prior line of therapy (BMS/BusinessWire press release; STAT News 2026-08-14 coverage; approval week of 2026-08-13): first-ever approval of a CELMoD (cereblon E3 ligase modulator) — a rationally engineered next-generation cereblon-binding molecular glue degrader in the thalidomide/lenalidomide/pomalidomide lineage that hijacks the cell’s ubiquitin-proteasome system to tag and destroy the myeloma-critical transcription factors Ikaros (IKZF1) and Aiolos (IKZF3); AND first cancer drug ever approved on a minimal residual disease-negative complete response (MRD-negative CR) endpoint — a stricter next-generation-sequencing readout requiring <1 myeloma cell per 10^5 bone marrow cells; approval based on the Phase 3 EXCALIBER-RRMM trial (n=939 randomized in total; primary efficacy population n=420 first randomized: 207 ZDd vs 213 DVd), showing MRD-negative CR at any time of 41% (95% CI 34–48%) with ZDd vs 21% (95% CI 15–27%) with DVd (p<0.0001), nearly a 2× improvement; PFS and OS still maturing as confirmatory endpoints; positions Zenbexus as BMS’s successor to Revlimid and Pomalyst (both losing patent exclusivity) with guided US sales >$1B/year by 2031 at $29,500 per 28-day cycle; strategically, first commercial validation for the targeted-degrader field with dozens of degrader programs in clinical development and FDA endorsement of MRD-negative CR that will shorten future myeloma and adjacent-heme trials. Google DeepMind releases Gemini 3.7 Flash (2026-08-13): workhorse-tier model tuned for coding and agentic workflows; DeepSWE v1.1 score jumps from 49.0% (3.6 Flash) to 65.3%; FrontierCode 1.1 Main from 34.4% to ~43.6%; introductory pricing $0.75/1M input tokens through 31 December 2026 — roughly half the blended cost of 3.6 Flash; maintains 1M-token context and multimodal input; not a frontier reasoning release but a substantial workhorse capability + pricing jump, which is the pattern that unlocks agentic use cases (like yesterday’s Claude/Riemann orchestration story) at scale. Dogs categorize distinct negative human emotions in the brain, not just positive-vs-negative (Hernández-Pérez, Concha, Andics, Bernal-Gamboa, Cuaya; University of Vienna + UNAM + Eötvös Loránd University; iScience 2026-08-07, doi:10.1016/j.isci.2026.116900): two awake-dog fMRI experiments — Exp. 1 (n=8) contrasted happy vs neutral human faces, Exp. 2 (n=12) contrasted happy, angry, fearful, and sad expressions; happy faces elicited stronger activity than neutral in a right-temporal cluster extending into the caudate nucleus (a reward-associated region previously shown to activate for familiar owner voice and preferred food odors); whole-brain multivariate patterns for anger, fear, and sadness were reliably distinguishable from each other — the first neuroimaging evidence dogs categorize distinct negative human emotions rather than lumping them as “human upset.”

item.title: Episode 50: A COVID variant trades grip for stealth
item.description: Antibody evasion and receptor binding of SARS-CoV-2 variants PQ.16.1.1 and RK.1 (He, Song, Guo, Yu, Yu, Jian, Shao, Cao; Changping Laboratory + Peking University; The Lancet Infectious Diseases, published 2026-08-13, doi:10.1016/S1473-3099(26)00429-9; preprint bioRxiv doi:10.64898/2026.07.21.739818): two SARS-CoV-2 sublineages descended from NB.1.8.1 have independently converged on the same D420N mutation in the spike receptor-binding domain (RBD) and now dominate the Asia-Pacific region; PQ.16.1.1 was designated a WHO Variant Under Monitoring on 27 July 2026; surface plasmon resonance shows PQ.16.1.1 RBD binds human ACE2 with KD ≈16.5 nM vs ≈8.22 nM for parental NB.1.8.1 — a ~2× loss of affinity — while pseudovirus neutralization assays show profound resistance to Class 1 neutralizing monoclonals and to convalescent plasma from Wuhan-Hu-1–primed individuals; textbook fitness trade-off — convergent sacrifice of receptor engagement for population-level immune escape — forecasting continued global spread and re-emphasizing surveillance of D420N-carrying lineages and neutralization coverage of updated boosters; abstract-only (bioRxiv body not yet rendered). Zipalertinib + platinum chemotherapy meets PFS primary endpoint at interim analysis in Phase 3 REZILIENT3 in first-line EGFR exon 20 insertion NSCLC (Taiho Pharmaceutical / Taiho Oncology / Cullinan Therapeutics press release, 12–13 August 2026; BioPharma Dive coverage): open-label randomized 285-patient trial of zipalertinib + platinum chemo vs chemo alone in previously untreated locally advanced/metastatic non-squamous NSCLC harboring EGFR ex20ins; Independent Data Monitoring Committee recommended early unblinding on statistically significant and clinically meaningful PFS benefit with manageable safety; hazard ratio not yet disclosed (full data at upcoming medical meeting), analyst commentary suggests effect cleared the pre-planned ~40% relative-risk-reduction bar; EGFR ex20ins is an underserved ~10% subset of EGFR-mutant NSCLC where classical EGFR TKIs (osimertinib) don't fit the drug pocket, current SOC is chemo ± Rybrevant (amivantamab; J&J) after mobocertinib's 2023 market withdrawal; establishes zipalertinib as a first-line oral contender and sets up a three-way race with ArriVent's firmonertinib (pivotal readout imminent) — likely to be decided on tolerability and route; sponsors to open first-line FDA discussions. Anthropic's unreleased Claude raises the proven lower bound on the fraction of Riemann zeta function zeros lying on the critical line from 41.6% to 67.2% (Anthropic announcement 10 August 2026; 35-page paper “More than Two Thirds of the Zeros of the Riemann Zeta Function Lie on the Critical Line” with formally verified Lean 4 proof, reviewed by Anthropic's Alpöge and Furman + external analytic number theorists Brian Conrey and Dan Goldston): claimed single largest jump in this century-old partial-result bound; method was agentic synthesis rather than novel mathematics — Claude combined Baluyot–Goldston–Suriajaya–Turnage-Butterbaugh's unconditional adaptation of Montgomery's 1973 techniques with Bombieri's 2000 paper, and performed the algebra to mesh them, a synthesis no human had executed despite both being in the public literature for years; ~31M output tokens across two sessions, ~60 subagents in Claude Code (2 core idea developers, 13 idea contributors, 30 exploratory dead-ends, 13 validators, 2 writers), 2,400 shell commands, ~36 hours; Anthropic explicitly cautions that these techniques are unlikely to lead to a full proof of the hypothesis — the significance is the demonstration that orchestrated subagent synthesis can produce frontier-technical output, with obvious portability to under-cross-referenced biomedical literature (drug repurposing, mechanistic biology, evidence pooling). Fossil evidence pushes origin of live birth in the mammalian lineage back ~95 million years (Gaetano et al., CONICET / lead author Leandro Gaetano; Frontiers in Mammal Science, published 2026-08-13): single juvenile specimen of Chiniquodon theotonicus — a cynodont proto-mammal — from ~236-million-year-old Middle Triassic rock in northwestern Argentina; team identified a neonatal line in the bone growth rings (the microscopic ring marking the abrupt metabolic reorganization at birth, present in placental mammals and absent/atypical in egg-layers) and back-calculated size at birth (~1.7 kg) vs death (~12 kg), giving birth mass ~14% of adult mass — squarely in the placental-mammal range and far above the <5% typical of egg-laying reptiles/birds; supports viviparity in at least one Triassic cynodont — pushing the earliest solid evidence of live birth in the mammalian line from ~140 Mya to ~236 Mya; authors note the caveat that Chiniquodon could represent an isolated evolutionary experiment and call for re-examination of other Triassic cynodont sites.

item.title: Episode 49: How COVID hijacks inflammation to spread
item.description: SARS-CoV-2 ORF8 promotes transmission by engaging an IFN-I–associated upper-respiratory-tract inflammatory response (Ciabattoni, Bartlett, McGrath, Frieman, Dittmann, Ortigoza; NYU Grossman School of Medicine + University of Maryland; bioRxiv 2026-08-11, doi:10.64898/2026.08.09.743817): infant-mouse model of intra-host SARS-CoV-2 transmission (littermate contact transmission is tractable in infant mice, unlike adult lab mice) comparing an isogenic ancestral rWA-1 (WA/2020) parent virus with a recombinant ∆ORF8 deletion mutant; ∆ORF8 mice show reduced infectious virus in URT tissues and nasal secretions and reduced index→contact transmission; ORF8-sufficient viruses induce greater macrophage recruitment, inflammatory cytokines, and type-I IFN signaling in URT; intranasal IFNβ supplementation partially rescues URT shedding and transmission in ∆ORF8-infected index mice, and blockade of the type-I IFN receptor (IFNAR) in rWA-1-infected index mice reduces both shedding and onward contact infection — two complementary directions establishing IFN-I signaling as a positive determinant of contagiousness rather than a purely protective response; naturally occurring ORF8 mutations phenocopy ∆ORF8; frames the URT innate-inflammatory secretory program as an axis SARS-CoV-2 exploits to increase host-to-host spread and introduces ORF8 status of circulating variants as a transmission-relevant surveillance dimension distinct from Spike; body-not-yet-rendered so pipeline is abstract-only. Jazz Pharmaceuticals to acquire Actio Biosciences for up to $1.32B for first-in-class KCNT1 potassium channel inhibitor (BioPharma Dive; deal announced 11 August 2026): $820M upfront + up to $500M in regulatory + sales milestones for privately-held San Diego biotech Actio Biosciences, expected to close Q4 2026, with concurrent spin-out of a separate Charcot-Marie-Tooth ion-channel-inhibitor company in which Jazz retains a minority stake; lead asset ABS-1230 is an oral first-in-class small-molecule inhibitor of KCNT1 (Slack), a sodium-activated potassium channel highly expressed on fast-spiking inhibitory interneurons; gain-of-function KCNT1 mutations cause KCNT1+ epilepsy, a rare genetic developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (~2,500 US patients, onset typically in infancy) with dozens-to-hundreds of daily seizures resistant to standard antiseizure drugs and severe developmental delay; mechanism resolves the paradox — over-active KCNT1 hyperpolarizes and silences inhibitory interneurons faster than excitatory neurons, releasing the brakes and driving runaway cortical excitation, so channel blockade restores balance; ongoing Phase 2 proof-of-concept in ~55 participants reported meaningful seizure reductions and drove Jazz’s acquisition; strategically extends Jazz’s rare-epilepsy franchise anchored by Epidiolex and is a template for mid-cap pharma acquisition of single-asset rare-disease biotechs at the human-signal inflection. siDiff: de novo target-conditioned siRNA design via efficacy-guided discrete masked diffusion (Yue, Zhang, Gao, Shu, Lai; Peking University; bioRxiv 2026-08-11, doi:10.64898/2026.08.11.744092): existing computational siRNA design relies on discriminative rescoring of pre-filtered candidate pools and generalizes poorly to novel gene targets; siDiff couples a discrete-masked-diffusion transformer that models the sequence distribution over functional siRNA duplexes with a mask-robust efficacy-prediction guidance model that steers sampling toward high-silencing candidates; inference-time three-stage biology-aware sampling adds structural candidate filtering (duplex foldability), dynamic unmasking guidance, and cluster-aware redundancy mitigation so returned hits are not near-copies of one sequence; evaluated across four datasets including the public Takayuki benchmark and three curated patent-derived sets, siDiff exceeds state-of-the-art discriminative and prior discrete-diffusion baselines by >30% relative hit-rate and preserves performance on out-of-distribution gene targets held out from training; positions diffusion + efficacy guidance as a more generalizable de novo design paradigm than discriminative pipelines at the front of the RNA-therapeutics pipeline — a natural follow-on to the Silence Therapeutics/divesiran Phase 2 story from yesterday’s episode; body-not-yet-rendered so pipeline is abstract-only. item.title: Episode 48: H5 lands in Australia
item.description: First confirmed detections and complete genomes of highly pathogenic avian influenza H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b on mainland Australia (Neave, Hair, Mileto, Mahar, Stevens, Davies, O’Dea, Iqbal, Ong, Hughes, Wang, Fox, Crowder, Gillies, Butler, Grimsey, McMahon, Gagliardi, Grech, Ford, Soul, Poon, Reid, Colling, McInnes, Burgess, Hodgson, Boulinier, Williams, Luczo, Bhardwaj, O’Brien, Eagles, Baele, Wong; CSIRO Australian Centre for Disease Preparedness + collaborators; bioRxiv 2026-08-10, doi:10.64898/2026.08.08.743700): H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b has caused a global panzootic since ~2020 (Europe → Americas → Antarctica/sub-Antarctic islands → U.S. dairy cattle in 2024) with Oceania as the last major HPAI-free region; two live seabirds — a brown skua and a southern giant petrel — found on the south coast of Western Australia in June 2026 tested positive; complete whole-genome sequencing of both viruses and time-calibrated phylogeographic analysis placed both most closely with H5N1 sequences from sub-Antarctic Southern Indian Ocean islands, clustering tightly with Heard Island (an uninhabited external Australian territory ~4,000 km SW of the mainland) genomes; ancestral location reconstruction identified Heard Island as the most probable source and the two WA viruses represent independent incursions rather than local onward transmission; no evidence of reassortment with endemic Australian avian influenza viruses, both viruses retain avian-like host markers and lack known antiviral-resistance substitutions; identifies a Southern Ocean pathway of recurrent H5N1 incursions into Australia and highlights migrating seabirds from sub-Antarctic islands as sentinel populations for national surveillance; body-not-yet-rendered so pipeline is abstract-only, but the phylogeographic result is the take. Silence Therapeutics reports positive Phase 2 SANRECO topline for divesiran in polycythemia vera (BioSpace press release; announced 10 August 2026): 48-patient, 36-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in phlebotomy-dependent PV patients dosed subcutaneously with divesiran 6 mg/kg every 6 weeks (Q6W) or every 12 weeks (Q12W); PV is a rare JAK2 V617F-driven myeloproliferative neoplasm (~160,000 U.S. patients) in which constitutive JAK2 signaling downstream of the erythropoietin receptor drives bone-marrow overproduction of red blood cells, elevating hematocrit and viscosity and increasing risk of stroke, MI, DVT, and PE; standard of care remains scheduled phlebotomy ± hydroxyurea/interferon/ruxolitinib; divesiran is a first-in-class siRNA targeting hepatic TMPRSS6 mRNA — TMPRSS6 normally suppresses hepcidin, the master iron-regulatory hormone; TMPRSS6 knockdown raises hepcidin, sequesters iron in enterocytes and macrophages, and starves erythropoiesis of the iron needed for hemoglobin synthesis, slowing red-cell production upstream of the JAK2 lesion; primary endpoint (avoidance of phlebotomy with Hct <45% over weeks 18–36) met with 88% response vs 19% placebo (p<0.0001; placebo-adjusted 69 pp); Q6W response 93.8%, Q12W response 81.3%; well tolerated (two grade 1 anemias, mechanistically consistent with iron restriction; infrequent, self-limiting injection-site reactions); Phase 3 planned to initiate 1H 2027; first Phase 2 proof-of-concept that drugging the hepcidin/iron-regulatory axis can treat a signaling-mutation-driven myeloproliferative neoplasm, with once-quarterly dosing potentially replacing scheduled bloodletting as the mainstay of PV management. Virtual-cell verification enables self-auditing AI discovery for immune rejuvenation (You, Fan, Li, Deng, Fu, Hu, Ren, Lu, Han, Shao, Zheng, Zhou, Kong, Chen, Liu, Tian; bioRxiv 2026-08-11, doi:10.64898/2026.08.04.742916): an agentic AI framework built on three verifiers designed to close the “verification gap” between AI-generated drug-discovery hypotheses and biological reality; (1) PACE, a phenotype verifier resolving immune aging into ten directionally scored, cell-type-resolved gene-set modules stable across four PBMC cohorts and outperforming five established aging clocks in an independent 434-donor elderly cohort; (2) CellQ, a multi-modal LLM virtual-cell verifier that compresses each single-cell transcriptome into eight discrete residual-vector-quantized tokens aligned to the language model’s vocabulary and attains state-of-the-art perturbation prediction, uniquely resolving weak module-level shifts differential-expression recovery misses; (3) an Analyzer–Planner–Auditor agent trio that audits and revises its own scoring logic against experimental results — in a 110-compound PBMC screen, the auditor detected that aged-down modules were more reversible than aged-up modules and rewrote the objective from equal-weight mean to a balance-constrained minimum, a self-correction that generalized to an independent 13-compound T-cell assay; frames the near-term shape of agentic AI-for-drug-discovery as hypothesis-and-audit rather than hypothesis-only, with the AI’s objective function itself updated by experiment; body-not-yet-rendered so pipeline is abstract-only. First evidence of maternal social transmission of “shelling” tool use in Queensland Indo-Pacific bottlenose dolphins (Levengood et al.; University of the Sunshine Coast; Marine Mammal Science 2026; phys.org 2026-08-11): boat + drone surveys July–October 2025 in the Great Sandy Marine Park documented two adult female Indo-Pacific bottlenose dolphins “shelling” — chasing fish into empty seashells (large gastropod/bivalve shells), lifting them to the surface, and tipping the water out to deliver prey into the mouth — and captured video of a calf picking up the mother’s dropped shell within minutes and handling it in the same manner, the first suggestive evidence of mother-to-calf social transmission for this behavior; the same technique was previously documented only in the Shark Bay, Western Australia population (>6,000 km away), indicating independent convergent invention of the same fish-trapping tool in geographically isolated populations; parallels the well-established mother-to-daughter social transmission of “sponging” in Shark Bay dolphins (using marine sponges to protect the rostrum while probing seafloor for camouflaged fish); reinforces cetacean cultural transmission as a widely distributed, matriline-anchored phenomenon and expands documented dolphin tool use to a second Australian population.

item.title: Episode 47: Heartland and Bourbon head west
item.description: First detections and complete genomes of Heartland virus (HRTV) and Bourbon virus (BRBV) from Amblyomma americanum ticks in Nebraska (Pella, Moody, Rodriguez, Chandler, Smith, Bartling, Herzog, Uhm, Stein, Iwen, McCutchen, Kenney, Hamik, Newman, Fauver; Nebraska DHHS + Nebraska Public Health Laboratory + University of Nebraska Medical Center; medRxiv 2026-08-10, doi:10.64898/2026.08.06.26359924): both HRTV (bunyavirus family, related to Rift Valley fever) and BRBV (thogotovirus, related to influenza but tick-borne) are emerging arboviruses vectored by the lone star tick; both were only described in the last 10–15 years (HRTV 2012 Missouri, BRBV 2014 Kansas) and have caused dozens of confirmed human cases with fatalities; historically anchored to MO/KS/TN/AR but expanding with lone star tick range; Nebraska DHHS added HRTV/BRBV screening to routine tick surveillance in 2024, PCR-positive pools from two eastern counties yielded 3 complete HRTV genomes and 1 complete BRBV genome via a newly developed amplicon-based whole-genome sequencing strategy; time-calibrated multi-segment phylogenetics placed the Nebraska HRTV genomes as a monophyletic cluster diverging from early-2000s Missouri lineages (co-timed with lone star tick range expansion into Nebraska), and the Nebraska BRBV genome sits on a long branch diverged from early-2010s sampled genomes (long branch = extensive unsampled tick-population diversity); topological concordance across genome segments indicates minimal reassortment; documents virus expansion to the western margin of lone star tick range ahead of any confirmed Nebraska human case — a preemptive surveillance win — and provides a portable amplicon-based sequencing method other state labs can adopt; clinical implication: HRTV and BRBV should now be on the differential for tick-exposed patients in the central US with fever, thrombocytopenia, leukopenia, and doxycycline non-response; body-not-yet-rendered so pipeline is abstract-only. Jazz Pharmaceuticals acquires Actio Biosciences for up to $1.32B for a first-in-class KCNT1 ion channel inhibitor (PRNewswire; deal announced 10 August 2026): $820M upfront + up to $500M in approval/sales milestones for privately-held San Diego biotech Actio Biosciences, expected to close Q4 2026, with concurrent spin-out of a separate rare-neurological company; lead asset ABS-1230 is an oral first-in-class small-molecule inhibitor of KCNT1 (Slack), a sodium-activated potassium channel expressed prominently on fast-spiking inhibitory interneurons; gain-of-function KCNT1 mutations cause KCNT1+ epilepsy, a rare genetic developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (~2,500 US patients, 80% seizure onset in infancy) characterized by dozens to hundreds of daily seizures resistant to all standard antiseizure drugs, severe developmental delay, and shortened life expectancy; mechanistically, over-active mutant KCNT1 hyperpolarizes and silences inhibitory interneurons faster than excitatory neurons, releasing the brakes on cortical circuits and driving runaway excitation — blocking KCNT1 restores circuit balance; preclinical work showed ABS-1230 inhibits KCNT1 across all evaluable pathogenic mutations, and an early proof-of-concept trial in children reported meaningful seizure reductions; ongoing KYRON trial is a ~55-patient Phase 1b/2a admitted to FDA’s Rare Disease Evidence Principles (RDEP) program supporting registrational filing; FDA Fast Track, Rare Pediatric Disease, and Orphan Drug designations; strategically extends Jazz’s rare-epilepsy franchise anchored by Epidiolex, with the deal shape (upfront-heavy but with meaningful contingent milestones) representative of modern mid-cap pharma acquisitions of single-asset rare-disease biotechs at the human-signal-not-yet-launch inflection point. AMIE (Video): Google Research + DeepMind Gemini-based multi-agent system for real-time clinical video consultations (Nagda, Lee, Thompson, Park + 36 co-authors; Google Research + Google DeepMind; arXiv 2026-08-10, arxiv:2608.09861): multimodal extension of the text-based AMIE (Articulate Medical Intelligence Explorer) system that had previously matched primary care physicians on written diagnostic-interview benchmarks; the Video configuration conducts a full video visit — history-taking, visual/auditory patient assessment, guided physical examination, differential diagnosis, and management plan — end-to-end; benchmarked via a randomized Objective Structured Clinical Examination (OSCE) with 30 primary care physicians (PCPs), 15 trained patient actors, and 100 clinical scenarios (mixed physical-exam-heavy and history-heavy), each scenario run twice in randomized order (AMIE Video vs PCP by video), blinded clinical evaluators scored history-taking, diagnostic accuracy, management appropriateness, and physical observation/examination; patient actors also scored satisfaction; blinded evaluators rated AMIE (Video) on par or better than PCPs across all four clinical-quality axes; patient actors preferred AMIE’s explanations but preferred human PCPs for rapport-building; remaining limitations include fine anatomical detail, subtle emotional nuance, and rapid movement (tremor/gait); first study evaluating a general-purpose LLM-based agent with audio-visual perception in the OSCE format that certifies human physicians and matching them on the four clinical-quality axes that matter; hints at near-term telemedicine division of labor with AI as diagnostic partner/first-contact triage layer and human physicians retaining rapport-heavy and emotionally attuned encounters. Why were there no tiny dinosaurs? (Lechki, Benson; Princeton + American Museum of Natural History; Evolution 2026, doi:10.1093/evolut/qpag117): non-avian dinosaurs occupied Earth’s terrestrial ecosystems for ~160 Myr and yet the smallest known non-avian dinosaur weighed ~450 g (roughly one pound / large rabbit); by contrast ~75% of extant mammal species and ~90% of extant bird species are smaller than that, and the smallest modern vertebrates (Etruscan shrew, bee hummingbird ~1.75–1.8 g, dwarf geckos ~0.15 g) are two orders of magnitude below the dinosaur floor; mathematical body-size evolution model based on energy uptake and reproductive tradeoffs was fit successfully to mammals, birds, and turtles but consistently over-predicts small dinosaurs across a wide range of physiological assumptions — physiology alone can’t explain the dinosaur size floor; the authors propose competition with small early mammals as the constraint (mammals occupied the small-bodied niches from below), mirroring the classic story that dinosaurs prevented mammals from getting large from above — two vertebrate radiations locking each other out of half the size spectrum for >100 Myr; birds escaped this ceiling via powered flight, opening new small-bodied niches (insect hawking, nectar feeding, canopy foraging) mammals hadn’t occupied, and radiated down to hummingbird sizes.

AMIE (Video): Google Research + DeepMind Gemini-based multi-agent system for real-time clinical video consultations (Nagda, Lee, Thompson, Park + 36 co-authors; Google Research + Google DeepMind; arXiv 2026-08-10, arxiv:2608.09861): multimodal extension of text-based AMIE (Articulate Medical Intelligence Explorer); Video configuration conducts end-to-end video visits — history, visual/auditory assessment, guided physical exam, differential, management plan; benchmarked via a randomized OSCE with 30 PCPs, 15 patient actors, 100 clinical scenarios (mixed physical-exam-heavy and history-heavy), each scenario run twice in randomized order (AMIE Video vs PCP by video), blinded clinical evaluators scored history-taking, diagnostic accuracy, management appropriateness, and physical observation/exam; blinded evaluators rated AMIE (Video) on par or better than PCPs across all four clinical-quality axes; patient actors preferred AMIE’s explanations, PCPs for rapport-building; remaining limitations in fine anatomical detail, subtle emotional cues, rapid movement; first LLM-based agent with audio-visual perception evaluated in the OSCE format and matching PCPs across the clinical-quality axes; hints at near-term telemedicine division of labor with AI as diagnostic partner/first-contact triage layer and human physicians retaining rapport-heavy encounters. Why were there no tiny dinosaurs? (Lechki, Benson; Princeton + American Museum of Natural History; Evolution 2026, doi:10.1093/evolut/qpag117): non-avian dinosaurs’ smallest species weighed ~450 g (~1 lb), while ~75% of extant mammals and ~90% of extant birds are smaller (with smallest modern vertebrates two orders of magnitude below the dinosaur floor); a body-size evolution model based on energetics and reproductive tradeoffs fits mammals, birds, turtles but consistently over-predicts small dinosaurs across wide physiological assumptions — physiology alone can’t explain the dinosaur size floor; the authors propose competition with small early mammals as the constraint (mammals occupied small-bodied niches from below), mirroring the classic story that dinosaurs kept mammals large from above — two vertebrate radiations locking each other out of half the size spectrum for >100 Myr; birds escaped this ceiling via powered flight into new small-bodied niches unoccupied by mammals.

item.title: Episode 46: H5 shows up in the neighborhood
item.description: Mucosal H5N1 antibody signal in the neighbors of industrial livestock operations (Pisanic, Kurowski, Carter, Salmeron, Pekosz, Gronvall, Heaney; Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health + Center for Health Security; medRxiv 2026-08-10, doi:10.64898/2026.08.06.26359901): saliva-based mucosal IgA and IgG against H5, H1, and H3 hemagglutinins were measured in North Carolina industrial livestock operation (ILO) workers, ILO neighbors with no occupational livestock contact, and metropolitan controls, sampled 2021–2022 (before the U.S. dairy-cattle H5N1 wave), and tested against zip-code-level poultry production intensity (PPI), swine production intensity (SPI), and a swine-specific fecal contamination marker (Pig-2-Bac DNA) on household surfaces; residing in the highest PPI/SPI tertile was associated with significantly elevated mucosal anti-H5 IgA even in residents with no farm work; per log10 increase in PPI, anti-H5 mucosal IgA rose 0.16 log10 (95% CI 0.06–0.27, p<0.005), and 0.10 per log10 SPI (p<0.005); Pig-2-Bac DNA detection on household surfaces added another 0.16 log10 (p<0.02); mucosal IgA is a footprint of antigen exposure (repeated low-dose exposure can generate it without productive infection), so this is an exposure-surface finding rather than a case count — but it demonstrates that ambient community H5 exposure around intensive poultry/swine operations is detectable and dose-responsive to production intensity, and that non-invasive saliva-based surveillance could sentinel-monitor community exposure to zoonotic influenza; body-not-yet-rendered so cross-reactivity between H5 and seasonal H1 hemagglutinin and any full breakdown of the exposure–infection gradient not yet assessable from the abstract. Braveheart Bio IPO $382.5M for BHB-1893 cardiac myosin inhibitor (BioPharma Dive; Nasdaq 6–7 August 2026, ticker BRVE): 21.25M shares priced at $18 by a Cambridge biotech founded 2024 by former HI-Bio executives, following a $185M Series A less than a year before going public; BHB-1893 is an oral cardiac myosin inhibitor licensed from Jiangsu Hengrui, positioned as a competitor to Bristol Myers Squibb’s Camzyos (mavacamten, first-in-class 2022) and Cytokinetics’ Myqorzo (aficamten) — the drug class dials down hypercontractility of the sarcomere (the actin/myosin contractile motor in cardiomyocytes), which is hyperactive in genetic hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) and drives wall thickening and outflow-tract obstruction that causes shortness of breath, chest pain, and sudden cardiac death; Braveheart claims better pharmacokinetics and a wider therapeutic window than Camzyos, potentially avoiding the ejection-fraction-reduction black-box monitoring; Hengrui is running the Phase 3 in China in obstructive HCM, Braveheart’s global Phase 3s in obstructive and non-obstructive HCM launch late 2026 / early 2027; 17th biotech IPO of 2026, in a year of structurally reopened biotech IPO markets financing late-stage de-risked clinical assets, and a template case of China-licensed asset + U.S. capital markets late-stage development. Pair representation scaling for inference-time conformational sampling in AlphaFold 3 and Boltz-2 (Suzuki, Amagasa; University of Tsukuba; bioRxiv 2026-08-09 v3, doi:10.64898/2026.01.23.701250): deep-learning protein structure predictors return a single dominant conformation, missing biologically important alternative states (open/closed enzyme conformations, inward/outward-facing membrane transporters, gating states of ion channels) that matter for mechanism and structure-based drug design; existing multi-state sampling approaches are heavy (perturbed/subsampled MSAs, many random seeds, alignment-based sampling); this paper multiplies the internal pair representation — the pairwise residue-residue distance/contact confidence tensor read by the Pairformer trunk — by a single scalar at inference time, with no retraining, no auxiliary model, no second forward pass; on 86 two-state targets (domain motions + membrane transporters) it broadens the conformational ensembles of both AlphaFold 3 and Boltz-2 and recovers alternative states default inference misses, most strongly in AlphaFold 3, with gains persisting on targets deposited after the training cutoff (rules out memorization) and without an MSA; approaches (does not beat) alignment-based sampling at a small fraction of the compute; predicted distance distributions shift directionally toward the experimentally observed alternative state, so it’s a directed modulation rather than random noise injection; interpretable low-cost knob on conformational ensembles from diffusion-based structure predictors; body-not-yet-rendered so ablation and coverage of harder multi-state cases (transporter cycling, allosteric ensembles) not yet assessable from the abstract. Dodo endocasts reveal enhanced olfaction, tactile beak, and crepuscular activity (University of Lethbridge + Natural History Museum Denmark; Zoological Journal of the Linnean Society 2026; phys.org 8 August 2026): high-resolution CT scans of three dodo (Raphus cucullatus) skulls including the only two complete specimens in existence (Natural History Museum Denmark, Oxford University Museum of Natural History); digital endocasts (brain-cavity reconstructions from imprints on the interior of the skull) were compared with modern pigeons and doves (the dodo’s closest living relatives); relative brain size and processing-region organization are consistent with modern pigeons — no evidence of reduced cognition, undermining the “stupid” folk story; enlarged olfactory bulbs and a large tactilely sensitive upper beak indicate the dodo foraged by smell and touch (rooting through leaf litter for fallen fruit) rather than by vision alone; visual-region morphology suggests activity extending into dawn and dusk rather than strictly diurnal; taken together, the dodo is a highly specialized foraging pigeon adapted to a predator-free Mauritius island niche — those adaptations became liabilities the moment humans landed, and first-contact accounts written by sailors are the source of the “stupid” misreading.

item.title: Episode 45: Cleaning up five million SARS-CoV-2 genomes
item.description: PhyCD, a phylogeny-aided contamination detector for pandemic-scale genome archives (Anoufa, Ly-Trong, Goldman, De Maio; European Bioinformatics Institute; bioRxiv 2026-08-07, doi:10.64898/2026.08.07.743473): consensus SARS-CoV-2 genomes deposited in public archives (~5M) can be corrupted by cross-sample contamination during batched sequencing, producing spurious mutations that distort phylogenetic and selection inferences; PhyCD masks positions with suspicious sequencing-read coverage drops, then uses pandemic-scale phylogenetic placement to flag genomes whose remaining mutations don’t fit anywhere sensibly on the global SARS-CoV-2 tree; applied to nearly 5 million public genomes it identified 10,942 putative contamination events under conservative parameters and flagged 64,753 individual substitutions for masking; provides open, rerunnable infrastructure to improve trust in the pandemic sequence archive on which essentially all SARS-CoV-2 evolutionary inference is based — body-not-yet-rendered so pipeline is abstract-only and false-positive rates against genuinely fast-evolving lineages (long-term chronic infections, cross-species transmission events) not yet assessable. Latigo Biotherapeutics IPO raises $346M for Nav1.8 non-opioid pain program (BioPharma Dive, Nasdaq listing 7 August 2026; ticker LTGO): 19.2M shares priced at $18 for gross proceeds $345.6M; Los Angeles biotech founded by Westlake BioPartners and staffed largely with former Amgen neuroscience pain-program employees; lead candidate LTG-001 is an oral, selective small-molecule inhibitor of Nav1.8, the peripheral-nerve-specific voltage-gated sodium channel that carries pain signals from nociceptive dorsal-root-ganglia neurons to the CNS; blocking Nav1.8 selectively cuts peripheral pain-signal transmission without touching cardiac, brain, or motor Nav subtypes and without engaging opioid receptors (no euphoria, no dependence); Phase 2 abdominoplasty trial met the SPID48 primary endpoint (sum of pain-intensity difference over 48 h) and the company will run a placebo-controlled Phase 3 bunionectomy trial — standard acute-pain registrational model; two additional pipeline candidates undisclosed; enters a target class validated by Vertex’s Journavx (suzetrigine, first Nav1.8-selective drug approved Jan 2025, ~$90M first-year sales) and Eli Lilly’s up-to-$1B SiteOne Therapeutics acquisition for chronic pain; Latigo is the 14th biotech to raise $250M+ in a US IPO in 2026 alone, matching the entire prior four-year total and reflecting a reopened biotech IPO window; addressable market is tens of millions of annual post-surgical opioid prescriptions in the US alone. Safety First: input screening for AI protein-design tools (Palmer, Teran, Wheeler, Yassif; Nuclear Threat Initiative-affiliated group; bioRxiv 2026-08-07, doi:10.64898/2026.08.04.740855): generative protein-binder models (RFdiffusion and successors) can now design novel binders whose sequences do not match anything in traditional homology databases, breaking BLAST-style biosecurity screening; framework flips the problem — screen the *target* (a natural human/pathogen protein pulled from a database, so structurally observable) rather than the AI-designed *binder*; the authors curate a database of 14,541 potentially harmful human proteoforms (7.1% of the human proteome) tagged by biosecurity risk level, then screen user-submitted binder targets via embeddings from Evolutionary Scale’s ESM-C (“Cambrian” release) protein language model; ESM-C achieves F1 >97% for detecting variants of known targets (on par with BLASTP) but outperforms BLASTP at distinguishing benign vs damaging mutations because it captures functional signal rather than raw sequence identity; flagging rates ~1% for bacterial/fungal/plant/viral proteins, 23% for human and 20% for mouse proteins weighted by publication frequency, 63% of antibody-patent targets are dual-use (therapeutically valuable and biosecurity-relevant); proposes a tiered trusted-access framework routing flagged targets to institutional-affiliation verification rather than hard block-listing, so legitimate therapeutic R&D isn’t shut out — first concrete, empirically calibrated, deployable biosecurity proposal for the generative-biology era — body-not-yet-rendered so pipeline is abstract-only. Newly described “coffee frog” endemic to Costa Rican coffee plantations (University of Costa Rica + CONICET Argentina; AFP via phys.org, 8 August 2026): small (<4 cm, ~1.6 inches) nocturnal tree frog, dark green with black spots, endemic to San Lorenzo de Tarrazú in Costa Rica’s central Pacific region; males call from coffee shrubs at night by inflating a translucent throat pouch that lights with each short, high-pitched note (the call is what led to the species being recognized as distinct); anthropophilic species using shade-grown coffee plantations as a partial substitute habitat for lost cloud-forest fragments; tadpoles develop in adjacent standing-water microhabitats and are highly sensitive to pesticide runoff, which travels through air, seeps through soil, and reaches the aquatic microhabitats; agricultural micro-drainage-level pesticide management directly determines species persistence; also a reminder that tropical vertebrate species descriptions in the 2020s still happen by fieldwork rather than only from museum specimens.

item.title: Episode 44: A pan-coronavirus vaccine hits its first big proof-of-concept
item.description: A bioRxiv preprint from Raiees Andrabi and Dennis Burton at Scripps (Zhou, Feng, He, Zhu, Yuan, Li, Zhang, Vo, Capozzola, Callaghan, Mishra, Avillion, Dueker, Liang, Roy Chowdhury, Nedellec, Lee, Allen, Walsh, Melo, McAnarney, Kumar, Rinaldi, Ferguson, Crispin, Ward, Irvine, Alameh, Weissman, Baric, Gralinski, Wilson, Burton, Andrabi; posted 2026-08-07, doi:10.64898/2026.08.06.743418) reports the first non-human primate proof-of-concept for a pan-betacoronavirus vaccine: an epitope-focused nanoparticle immunogen displaying the conserved S2 stem-helix region of the spike fusion machinery (a broadly-neutralizing epitope shared across sarbecoviruses, merbecoviruses, and embecoviruses but partially occluded on native spike) — immunization of rhesus macaques (alone or prime-boosted with a SARS-CoV-2 BA.1 spike mRNA) elicited cross-reactive antibody responses against all three betacoronavirus subgenera and neutralized SARS-CoV-2, multiple variants, additional sarbecoviruses, and MERS-CoV; vaccine-elicited monoclonal antibodies protected against both SARS-CoV-2 and MERS-CoV in vivo; structural analyses show conserved features between rhesus and rare-human stem-helix bnAbs (translational bridge); establishes epitope-focused nanoparticle immunogens as a route to preemptive pan-coronavirus vaccination rather than reactive R-B-D updates — posted body-not-yet-rendered so abstract-only. FDA accelerated approval of Replimune Tudriqev (vusolimogene oderparepvec-wtpg, RP1) + nivolumab for post-anti-PD-1 unresectable advanced cutaneous melanoma (FDA 6 August 2026, PDUFA date 2 August, adcom 30 July 10-3 in favor after two prior CRLs July 2025 and April 2026): first oncolytic viral therapy approved in the US since Amgen’s 2015 Imlygic; genetically engineered herpes simplex virus type 1 expressing GM-CSF (immune recruitment) + GALV-derived fusogenic glycoprotein (syncytial tumor-cell fusion); intratumoral injection every 2 weeks × 8 doses with intravenous nivolumab starting week 3; single-arm Phase 2 IGNYTE trial n=140 (efficacy-evaluable n=91 with at least one non-injected lesion; 80% stage IV, 54% PD-L1 negative): ORR 24.2% central review, mDOR 14.1 months, broader-cohort ORR 33.6%, 15% CR rate, 3-year OS 47.8% overall (83.5% among responders); AEs predominantly grade 1-2 (fatigue, pyrexia, chills, nausea, injection-site reactions), serious AEs 35%, label warnings for herpetic infection and injection-related visceral injury; confirmatory Phase 3 IGNYTE-3 ~400 patients due ~2030 (accelerated approval may be withdrawn if it misses); regulatory reversal validates oncolytic virus + checkpoint inhibitor combination platform for post-standard-of-care oncology unmet need. Vir3D structure-aware deep learning for influenza antigenicity and vaccine strain selection (Li, Zhou, Xiao, Xu, Jia, Zhao, Chen, Li, Peng, Zhu, Liu, Shang, Kong; Northwestern Polytechnical University; bioRxiv 2026-08-07, doi:10.64898/2026.08.02.742372): uses ESMFold-derived 3D structural embeddings of hemagglutinin (H3 human + highly pathogenic H5 avian subtypes) to predict pairwise antigenic distances from sequence alone; discriminates antigenic variants, delineates key structural residues driving immune evasion; decade-long retrospective analysis showed Vir3D-prioritized vaccine strains consistently achieve broader antigenic coverage of circulating strains than WHO recommendations; correctly predicted the U.S. dairy cattle H5N1 (TX/24) remains antigenically stable relative to clade 2.3.4.4b vaccine strains, wet-lab confirmed by hemagglutination inhibition assay; positions foundation-model-derived structure prediction as a reusable feature extractor for pandemic preparedness and vaccine strain recommendation — body-not-yet-rendered so abstract-only. Rediscovered Denmark Megalodon vertebrae (Shimada, Elstrup, Lauridsen, Sørensen, Siversson; DePaul University + Aarhus University + Western Australian Museum; Palaeontologia Electronica 2026, doi:10.26879/1674): several enormous Otodus megalodon vertebrae from the Upper Miocene Gram Formation in Denmark (~11 Mya) rediscovered on a shelf at the Natural History Museum of Denmark after being recorded as damaged or lost in the 1989 collection move from the Geological Museum in Copenhagen to the Museum of Southern Jutland; largest vertebra 23 cm diameter (9 inches), the largest O. megalodon vertebra ever measured; scaling from vertebral diameter to body length (much more reliable than tooth-based estimates because vertebrae actually fossilize and scale predictably with body size) puts the animal at >24 m (79 ft) length and consistent with a near-century lifespan; growth-ring back-calculation from a single-individual set puts newborn Megalodon size at ~3.6 m (12 ft) — larger than most adult great white sharks; illustrates high-value paleontology done in museum collections rather than the field.

item.title: Episode 43: Evolutionary checkmate for pan-drug-resistant Pseudomonas
item.description: A bioRxiv preprint from Sam Diggle’s group at Georgia Tech with Kendra Rumbaugh’s lab at Texas Tech (Estrada, Campbell, Welch, Smith, Goldberg, Rumbaugh, Diggle; posted 2026-08-06, doi:10.64898/2026.08.04.742823) shows that R-pyocins — phage-tail-derived narrow-spectrum bactericidal particles — can be used as evolutionary selective pressure to force pan-drug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa into an “evolutionary checkmate”: escape from R-pyocin killing requires 250–388 kb chromosomal deletions spanning galU (LPS core biosynthesis, the R-pyocin receptor), hmgA (pyomelanin/brown-colony phenotype), and the mexXY multidrug efflux operon co-located in a conserved genomic region; loss of galU confers R-pyocin resistance, concurrent excision of mexXY produces collateral sensitivity to aminoglycosides, and the same deletions strip large virulence and biofilm operons (hcnABC, exoY, phzABCDEFG, cup); tested on laboratory strains PAO1 and PAK and on clinical pan-drug-resistant wound isolate MRSN 6220; brown escape mutants are non-lethal in Galleria mellonella and produce a 3-log reduction in murine chronic-wound bacterial load with gentamicin treatment; the strategy uses resistance evolution as a lever rather than fighting it and offers a topical wound-preconditioning framework for otherwise-untreatable PDR Pseudomonas infections. Two first-in-class FDA approvals landed on 5 August 2026: (1) Moderna mFlusiva (mRNA-1010) — the first mRNA-based seasonal influenza vaccine ever licensed in the US, approved for adults ≥50 (accelerated approval for ≥65 subgroup); trivalent formulation encoding hemagglutinin of A/H1N1, A/H3N2, and B/Victoria (Yamagata dropped following WHO 2024 recommendation and the pandemic-era Yamagata extinction); Phase 3 P304 trial (n=40,805 adults ≥50 across 11 countries, NEJM 2026; 12.5 μg HA-mRNA per strain vs standard-dose licensed comparator) showed 26.6% relative vaccine efficacy vs standard dose against PCR-confirmed ILI (95% CI 16.7–35.4), 27.4% in ≥65 subgroup, strain-specific rVE 29.6% (H1N1), 22.2% (H3N2), 29.1% (B/Victoria); platform advantage is collapsing the ~9-month WHO strain-selection lead time by removing egg-based manufacturing. (2) Takeda ORZEYFUL (oveporexton, TAK-861) — first-ever orexin receptor 2 (OX2R) agonist, approved for narcolepsy type 1 in adults; NT1 (~120,000 US patients) is defined by autoimmune loss of hypothalamic orexin/hypocretin neurons and the resulting cataplexy + excessive daytime sleepiness; existing therapies (modafinil, sodium oxybate, pitolisant, solriamfetol) all substitute at other arousal pathways; oveporexton directly activates OX2R to restore the missing wake signal; Phase 3 FirstLight (TAK-861-3001, n=168) + RadiantLight (TAK-861-3002, n=105) met all primary + secondary endpoints at week 12 — MWT sleep latency into the ≥20 min normal range at 2 mg BID, ~85% of treated patients achieved ESS ≤10, weekly cataplexy rate significantly reduced; AEs consistent with wake system activation (insomnia 60% vs 1% placebo, urinary frequency 58% vs 5%, asymptomatic CPK >5×ULN in 11% vs 5%); DEA scheduling expected within 90 days; validates orexin agonism as a receptor-replacement strategy for a defined neuropeptide-deficiency disease. And a Nature Communications paper (Gomez, Pitnick, Dorus + University of Siena + University of Szeged; Syracuse University; published 2 August 2026) maps sperm cooperation across arthropod phylogeny over ~600 Myr of evolution: sperm conjugation (physical binding of sperm from a single individual into coordinated bundles) and sperm-associated material (secreted membrane-bound packaging that structures sperm together) are widespread across arthropods and have evolved and been lost independently many times; the reconstructed ancestor of all insects had conjugated sperm; challenges the “sperm race” individual-competition model as a mammal-derived special case rather than a general rule, with candidate selective pressures including faster transit through female reproductive tract geometry, resistance to displacement by later matings, and cargo delivery.

item.title: Episode 42: Why influenza B Yamagata seems to have gone extinct
item.description: A medRxiv preprint from Manuel Antonio Gutierrez in Pej Rohani’s group at the University of Georgia (Gutierrez, Page, Tompkins, Rohani; posted 5 August 2026, doi:10.64898/2026.08.03.26359614) analyzes a status-based two-strain SIRS model with asymmetric cross-immunity, strain-specific transmission/recovery rates, and waning immunity to derive explicit invasion thresholds and closed-form coexistence-equilibrium expressions; the central result is that a transient reduction in transmission can push a stably coexisting strain pair across an invasion boundary and drive the weaker strain extinct even after transmission recovers — applied to influenza B, this offers a parsimonious explanation for the apparent extinction of the Yamagata lineage during the COVID-19 pandemic (Yamagata has had no confirmed detections since ~2020, and the WHO in 2024 recommended dropping the Yamagata component from trivalent/quadrivalent seasonal flu vaccines); reframes flu B lineage loss not as a numerical drop that failed to bounce back but as a phase transition induced by a brief transmission shock, with broader implication that large respiratory-transmission interventions can permanently reshape which competing strains circulate afterward. Moderna announced initiation of the Phase 1 clinical trial of mRNA-1469, its investigational Bundibugyo ebolavirus mRNA vaccine (first participants dosed 4 August 2026 following Health Canada authorization; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07737717): ~80 healthy adult participants across three Canadian sites evaluating safety, tolerability, and immunogenicity; CEPI committed up to $50M for preclinical + Phase 1 work, and Moderna pledged a minimum of 500,000 doses to LMICs at access pricing if the vaccine is licensed; delivered against an ongoing WHO-declared PHEIC Bundibugyo outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo with 3,748 confirmed cases and 1,657 deaths as of 1 August 2026 (second-largest Ebola outbreak on record) — against which the two licensed ebolavirus vaccines (Merck Ervebo and J&J Zabdeno/Mvabea, both Zaire ebolavirus-specific) are being used off-label without demonstrated Bundibugyo cross-protection; mRNA-1469 encodes the Bundibugyo glycoprotein on the same LNP-mRNA architecture as Moderna’s COVID vaccine and is the first real-world stress test of the mRNA platform against a filovirus surface glycoprotein rather than a coronavirus spike. And a Gondwana Research paper (Matt White, University of New England, with Dean Lomax and colleagues, summer 2026) describes the “Bag of Bones” specimen — a 6–7 m ichthyosaur (Platypterygius australis) from a public fossicking site near Richmond, Queensland, in Early Cretaceous (~100 Ma) Eromanga Sea deposits — recovered by public finders August 2019 and completed by Kronosaurus Korner curator Kevin Petersen in 2022: synchrotron CT scanning at ANSTO of nodules in the ichthyosaur’s stomach cavity revealed pterosaur jaw fragments alongside fish, belemnite, and shell remains, while the skeleton itself bears crushing bite marks consistent with attack/scavenging by the giant pliosaur Kronosaurus queenslandicus — the first single fossil to preserve three trophic levels (pterosaur eaten by ichthyosaur eaten by pliosaur). No AI in biomedicine or AI tools segment today: nothing in the last 24–48 h rose above the noise.

item.title: Episode 41: The biggest Cyclospora outbreak in U.S. history
item.description: The CDC’s Taco Bell/Taylor Farms iceberg-lettuce Cyclospora outbreak update (CDC 4 August 2026): >10,000 laboratory-confirmed domestic cases nationally since 1 May 2026, plus ~12,000 additional cases awaiting confirmation; Michigan is the epicenter with state-level count above 10,000 and >190 hospitalizations; the outbreak’s first two deaths (both Michigan) were reported 3 August; nine-state cluster spans Illinois, Indiana, Kansas, Kentucky, Michigan, Ohio, Oklahoma, Pennsylvania, West Virginia; Taylor Farms de México recalled iceberg lettuce from central Mexican operations on 17 July 2026 after FDA trace investigation; no product sample has tested positive for Cyclospora, and the epidemiological identification rests on food-history interviews plus partial CDC genotyping because Cyclospora cayetanensis (Apicomplexa coccidian) cannot be cultured and only environmentally-matured oocysts (days to weeks post-shedding, temperature/moisture dependent) are infectious — documents the surveillance blind spot for uncultivable foodborne parasites vs bacterial PulseNet whole-genome pipelines. Otsuka VOYXACT (sibeprenlimab-szsi) VISIONARY Phase 3 24-month eGFR results (Otsuka press release 4 August 2026, on primary IgA nephropathy): eGFR annualized slope +0.3 mL/min/1.73 m²/year sibeprenlimab vs −4.2 placebo (treatment effect +4.5 mL/min/1.73 m²/year, p<0.0001); LS-mean eGFR change from baseline at 24 months +1.3 vs −7.9 (∆ = +9.2 mL/min/1.73 m²); adverse events 90.7% vs 90.0%, infections/infestations 51.4% vs 51.0%, injection-site reactions 35.1% vs 32.2%; serious infections *lower* on sibeprenlimab 1.9% vs 4.0%; sibeprenlimab is a humanized mAb targeting APRIL (TNF-superfamily cytokine, receptors BCMA/TACI) blocking pathogenic Gd-IgA1 production; FDA accelerated approval granted 25 November 2025 on 9-month proteinuria; the 24-month eGFR slope meets KDIGO physiologic-decline threshold and supports Otsuka’s rolling sBLA for full traditional approval; competitive pipeline includes Novartis zigakibart (Phase 3, anti-APRIL) and Vera Therapeutics atacicept (dual APRIL+BAFF). Pathos AI package of deals (Pathos AI press release + Fierce Biotech/Endpoints/MedCity News, 3–4 August 2026): $125M upfront + up to $2.1B in milestones plus tiered royalties for global (ex-Greater China) rights to Alphamab Oncology’s JSKN016 — a TROP2/HER3 bispecific antibody-drug conjugate in Phase 3 in China; simultaneous collaboration with AstraZeneca on AZD4241 (undisclosed terms), an estrogen-receptor-directed protein degrader for breast cancer, with Pathos running the early clinical program; and a new Series E of up to $300M announced. CEO Iker Huerga positions the company’s AI platform Foundry as “thousands of AI agents that work in parallel” on drug/patient-matching + trial design; the deals confirm the actual AI-in-drug-discovery business model that is finding funding — licensing human-designed molecules from Chinese biotech and large pharma and applying AI to clinical development, not designing new molecules de novo. And a Nature paper (Liu, Lustri, Mai, Williams et al., Yunnan University + University of Leicester, doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10713-2) describes Urokodia aequalis from the Chengjiang biota (Yunnan Province, southern China): a 2–3 cm early Cambrian marine euarthropod with a seven-segmented head, sclerotized hypostome, large stalked eyes, pincer-like appendages behind the eyes, and biramous trunk appendages with overlapping exite flaps; X-ray microtomography resolves the 3D anatomy; the pincer-like appendages are the earliest known bridge structure between multisegmented appendages and true chelicerae, and the trunk exite flaps support a megacheiran origin of book gills — identifying Urokodia as the earliest known ancestor of the venom-delivering fangs of spiders (Chelicerata, 100,000+ species) and of the respiratory apparatus of horseshoe crabs.

Urokodia aequalis reveals the origin of chelicerae and book gills (Liu, Lustri, Mai, Williams, Liu, Tang, Harvey, Hou, Yunnan University + University of Leicester, Nature 2026, doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10713-2): 2–3 cm early Cambrian marine euarthropod from the Chengjiang biota, Yunnan Province, southern China, 518 Mya; paper published 1 July 2026 on the 42nd anniversary of the Chengjiang site’s discovery; X-ray microtomography resolves 3D anatomy including a seven-segmented head with sclerotized hypostome, large stalked eyes, pincer-like appendages positioned just behind the eyes, and biramous trunk appendages with overlapping exite flaps; the pincer-like appendages are the earliest known bridge structure between multisegmented appendages and true chelicerae — ancestral to the venom-delivering fangs of every living spider and the pincers of scorpions (Chelicerata, >100,000 species); the trunk exite flaps support a megacheiran origin of book gills, the respiratory apparatus retained in living horseshoe crabs and derived to book lungs in terrestrial arachnids.

item.title: Episode 40: A one-shot pan-H5N1 vaccine, and citations that fool doctors
item.description: A bioRxiv preprint (Elsayed, Barre, Rahmani et al.; corresponding authors Adolfo García-Sastre, Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai, and Luis Martínez-Sobrido, Texas Biomedical Research Institute; posted 3 August 2026, doi:10.64898/2026.08.02.742385) describes a one-shot multivalent live-attenuated influenza vaccine (LAIV) built on the temperature-sensitive/cold-adapted/attenuated A/Ann Arbor/6/1960 master donor virus (same backbone as FluMist), carrying HA+NA glycoproteins from H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b (A/Louisiana/12/2024), clade 2.3.2.1a (A/Victoria/149/2024), and clade 2.3.2.1e (A/Cambodia/2302009/2023); a single intranasal dose in C57BL/6 mice elicited humoral responses broadly cross-reactive against antigens from all three clades and provided complete protection against homologous viral challenge — establishes proof-of-concept for pan-H5N1 coverage from a single LAIV, directly relevant to the ongoing 2.3.4.4b panzootic (yesterday’s South Australia greater crested tern mass mortality). The FDA on 31 July 2026 approved Pluvicto (lutetium Lu-177 vipivotide tetraxetan; Novartis) with an androgen-receptor pathway inhibitor for adults with PSMA-positive metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer — the third indication expansion for the PSMA-targeted β-emitting radioligand (previously: 2022 mCRPC post-chemo, 2025 mCRPC pre-chemo), nearly doubling the eligible metastatic-prostate-cancer population; Phase 3 PSMAddition (N=1,144 randomized 1:1 Pluvicto + ADT + ARPI vs ADT + ARPI): primary endpoint rPFS HR 0.72 (95% CI 0.58-0.90; ~28% reduction), OS trend HR 0.80 (0.63-1.01, immature); dosing 7.4 GBq every 6 weeks × 6; grade ≥3 AEs 50.7% vs 43%; rationale is early treatment intensification since ~1/3 of mHSPC patients never reach undetectable PSA on standard doublet and ~half progress within 20 months; Lu-177 manufacturing capacity remains a bottleneck. An arXiv paper from Titus J. Brinker’s group at DKFZ Heidelberg with clinicians from Medical University of Vienna, TU Dresden, and Pontifical Catholic University of Chile (Chanda, Wies, Schramm et al.; arXiv:2608.00817, 1 August 2026) tested CORA, an agentic retrieval-augmented LLM with source-linked citations, on 46 physicians answering clinical questions with and without assistance: unaided accuracy 70.8% vs 82.6% with CORA; citation-supported answers correct 87.7% of the time vs 65.5% for uncited; citation-adoption asymmetry — when correct answers were citation-supported, physician adoption rose 34% → 76.9%, but when incorrect answers were citation-supported, physician resistance to the wrong answer collapsed 92% → 34.8%; documents a grounding-dependent safety risk in current retrieval-augmented clinical LLMs (dermatology, ambient scribes, EHR integrations) — citations function as a trust amplifier that operates on wrong answers as strongly as on right ones. And a ZooKeys taxonomy paper (Hu, Solodovnikov, Natural History Museum of Denmark and University of Copenhagen; ZooKeys 1281:247-264, doi:10.3897/zookeys.1281.198593) erects the new rove-beetle genus Luffy (family Staphylinidae, subfamily Staphylininae, subtribe Staphylinina) with two species from Asian montane broadleaf forest — L. schillhammeri (Yunnan Province, China) and L. nika (Louang Namtha, northern Laos) — distinguished by unusually elongated, slender mandibles, antennae, and maxillary palps that inspired the naming after Monkey D. Luffy of One Piece; recovered as sister to the Eucibdelus lineage, resolving a phylogenetic gap in the Ocypus-group.

item.title: Episode 39: Australia's H5N1 outbreak claims its first native seabirds
item.description: South Australia's Primary Industries and Regions department confirmed on 2 August 2026 the first mass mortality event of native wildlife in Australia's ongoing H5N1 (clade 2.3.4.4b, genotype B3.2) outbreak: aerial surveillance on Friday 1 August counted 49 dead and 35 sick greater crested terns on Baudin Rocks, a protected islet ~200 km southeast of Adelaide; South Australia now at 40 confirmed positives. Australia had been the last continent free of the current H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b panzootic until the 14 June 2026 detection in a brown skua at Cape Le Grand National Park (Western Australia), sequenced and confirmed by CSIRO’s Australian Centre for Disease Preparedness. Colonial seabird ecology at Baudin Rocks parallels the die-off pattern that killed ~40% of Peruvian pelicans on the Chilean coast (2022) and decimated South Georgia penguin colonies; silver-gull detections are the pathway of greatest concern for spillover into commercial poultry. Financial Times reported over the weekend of 2-3 August that AstraZeneca held early-stage exploratory talks with Bristol Myers Squibb about a potential all-stock combination that would be the largest pharma merger ever (~$400B combined market cap; AZ ~$196B, BMS ~$133B); AstraZeneca -~4% and BMS +~6% in pre-market Monday trading. Analyst consensus (BMO, Jefferies) is that the deal is unlikely to materialize due to structural antitrust exposure in advanced non-small-cell lung cancer, where BMS’s Opdivo ($10B in lung sales 2025) and AstraZeneca’s Imfinzi ($6B) are direct competitors on PD-(L)1 checkpoint blockade — a problem not solvable by divestiture. Strategic rationale is defensive against parallel late-decade patent cliffs (Farxiga/Tagrisso for AZ; Revlimid for BMS); reference precedent is AZ’s 2014 rejection of Pfizer’s hostile bid, with CEO Pascal Soriot vindicated by pipeline execution. A bioRxiv preprint from Arora, Chen, Du, Marks, Church (Harvard Medical School, v2 updated 3 August 2026) introduces PG-LLM, a benchmark of 217 ProteinGym variant-ranking tasks evaluating 13 general-purpose language models (LLMs) tool-free against 95 published protein predictors: Claude Opus 5 leads the LLM leaderboard at Spearman ρ=0.406, GPT-5.6 Sol at 0.402, both approaching ESM-2-650M (0.411) and outperforming 49/95 specialists (41/46 sequence-only) but well below leading specialist VenusREM (0.523); performance is robust to alignment depth (LLMs do not need deep MSAs), improves with test-time compute up to a plateau, and is confirmed on 59 held-out DMS assays first published after January 2026 to rule out training-set contamination; establishes general-purpose LLMs as viable variant-prioritization tools particularly for orphan proteins where specialist evolutionary methods fail. And a Nature Ecology and Evolution paper from Jake Berv (Weeks lab, U-Michigan) with Fouhey lab (NYU) uses Skelevision, a computer vision model that extracts precise anatomical measurements from ~15,000 photographed museum bird skeletons in ~45 s each, to accumulate ~170,000 skeletal measurements across ~2,000 passerine (songbird) species; a novel multivariate method (Bifrost) tests whole-body-plan evolution over Passeriformes’ ~45 Myr history and identifies a major evolutionary burst ~35 Mya coinciding with the Eocene-Oligocene transition and Antarctic ice-sheet formation, plus a Miocene ~15 Mya slowdown as climate stabilized — quantitative field-scale support for Gould-Eldredge punctuated equilibrium in vertebrate morphology.
