item.title: Episode 38: The heart drug that hit its target and missed anyway
item.description: A bioRxiv preprint from Kassabian, Al Khoury, Araj, Tokajian (Lebanese American University, Byblos) documents the first within-host succession from an OXA-48-family carbapenemase to an NDM-type in clonal ST361 Escherichia coli recovered 25 days apart from sequential UTI and bloodstream infection in one patient (28 core-genome SNPs apart, clonally identical). The first isolate carried blaOXA-1207 on a conjugative IncFII(pCoo)/ColKP3 plasmid; the second had lost it and gained blaNDM-4 on a globally disseminated IncX3 backbone nearly identical to pJEG027 — a plasmid-level swap rather than in-place gene evolution; phenotype shifted from imipenem/meropenem-susceptible + ceftazidime-avibactam-susceptible to uniform high-level carbapenem resistance and ceftazidime-avibactam-resistant, so continuity-of-empiric-therapy assumptions across sequential CRE isolates would have failed. Novo Nordisk announced Friday 31 July 2026 that its Phase 3 ZEUS trial of ziltivekimab — a monthly anti-IL-6 monoclonal (from the 2021 $1.9B Corvidia acquisition) — missed its primary MACE endpoint in >6,300 patients with atherosclerotic CVD + CKD + inflammation (hs-CRP elevated) with HR 0.99 (95% CI 0.88-1.11) despite achieving expected pharmacodynamic effect (free IL-6 and hs-CRP dropped); serious infections more common on ziltivekimab; the failure is the first randomized challenge to the inflammation hypothesis of atherosclerosis after CANTOS (canakinumab, IL-1β upstream, 2017) validated it, and it reopens the CRP-as-marker-vs-causal-driver question; stock down ~9%; HERMES (HFpEF) and ARTEMIS (post-MI) Phase 3 readouts still expected H1 2027. And a Journal of Systematic Palaeontology paper from Paul Barrett and colleagues (Natural History Museum London, with Zimbabwean/South African collaborators) names Musango matusadonaensis, the fifth dinosaur ever formally described from Zimbabwe: an early sauropodomorph from the ~210 Ma Late Triassic recovered on the shores of Lake Kariba in 2018, ~4.5 m long, ~222 kg, lightly built and probably bipedal, ~8 years old and nearly fully grown, bones preserve a healed serious injury or infection; co-occurs at the same locality with the earlier-described stockier Musankwa sanyatiensis — two coexisting sauropodomorphs argue for greater Late Triassic dinosaur diversity in southern Africa than the fossil record had been recording.

item.title: Episode 37: The cow udder could be a flu mixing vessel
item.description: An Emerging Microbes & Infections paper from Fritsch, Arora, Becher and colleagues (University of Veterinary Medicine Hannover) builds a scalable bovine mammary gland organoid model from primary dairy-cow udder epithelium and infects it with a panel of five phylogenetically diverse influenza A viruses. Contemporary US dairy H5N1 (A/cattle/Texas/063224-24-1/2024), swine-origin H1N1 (2006), and human pandemic H1N1 (2009) all replicate to ~10^7 TCID50/mL by 48 hpi — the mammalian H1N1 strains match H5N1 in efficiency in cow udder tissue; avian H7N7 replicates productively at somewhat lower titers; only H9N2 shows restricted, near-abortive replication. SNA and MAL-II lectin staining shows bovine mammary epithelium abundantly displays both α2,3 and α2,6 sialic-acid linkages — reframing the cow udder as a broadly permissive IAV niche with plausible reassortment potential, not an H5N1-specific tissue oddity. Replimune's RP1 (vusolimogene oderparepvec) — an HSV-1-based oncolytic virus engineered to carry the GALV-GP-R- fusogen and human GM-CSF — cleared the FDA Cellular, Tissue & Gene Therapies Advisory Committee 10-3 on 30 July 2026 that the IGNYTE trial is evaluable and clinically meaningful in anti-PD-1-refractory advanced melanoma (n=140, ORR 32.9-38.7%, 15% complete responses, median DOR >35 months, Grade 3+ AEs 12.8%); PDUFA date 2 August 2026 after two prior CRLs (July 2025 and April 2026), with confirmatory IGNYTE-3 enrolling as a randomized study — if approved, first oncolytic virus to reach the US market since Amgen's T-VEC (2015). Google DeepMind has disbanded the AlphaFold team less than a year after John Jumper's Nobel: staff redistributed across Gemini, Isomorphic Labs, and other DeepMind projects; ~25% left Google entirely; Jumper and coauthors Jonas Adler and Alexander Pritzel moved to Anthropic in June 2026. Pushmeet Kohli framed the shift as away from grand-challenge dedicated teams and toward Gemini-based general science assistants; AlphaFold Server and databases remain online; a concurrent bioRxiv preprint (Solanki et al., 2026-07-31) benchmarking AlphaFold3 antibody-antigen prediction across 3,401 complexes finds systematic epitope hallucination, complicating any "solved" framing of protein-structure prediction. And a Scientific Reports paper from Niemiller and colleagues (University of Alabama in Huntsville / Auburn / U Alabama / Mississippi State) describes a new genus of cave-obligate fish — Demogorgonichthys arcanus (Amblyopsidae) — from Bobcat Cave under Redstone Arsenal in northern Alabama; distinguished from co-occurring Typhlichthys subterraneus by CT-based skeletal anatomy plus mitochondrial and nuclear sequencing, in syntopy despite deep phylogenetic distance — textbook convergent cavefish evolution in a single karst pool.

Replimune RP1 FDA CTGT Advisory Committee 10-3 favorable vote (30 July 2026) ahead of 2 August PDUFA in anti-PD-1-refractory advanced melanoma: RP1 is HSV-1 based, engineered to express GALV-GP-R- fusogen (drives cell-cell fusion and syncytial death of infected tumor cells) and GM-CSF (recruits antigen-presenting cells to release tumor antigens for downstream T-cell priming); IGNYTE trial n=140 in anti-PD-1 progressors, ORR 32.9-38.7% by RECIST v1.1, 15% complete responses, median DOR >35 months, Grade 3+ AEs 12.8%, no drug-related deaths; two prior CRLs (July 2025 and April 2026) cited single-arm design as inadequate; confirmatory IGNYTE-3 randomized trial already enrolling; if approved, first oncolytic virus on the US market since Amgen's T-VEC (2015) and a template for OV + checkpoint-inhibitor combinations in other indications. Demogorgonichthys arcanus, a new genus of cave-obligate amblyopsid fish from Bobcat Cave under Redstone Arsenal (Niemiller, Armbruster, Hart, Sandel et al., UAH/Auburn/U Alabama/Mississippi State, Scientific Reports 2026-07-27): eyeless, colorless, faintly-electric-blue-in-life, hunchbacked with an elongated flattened snout; distinguished from co-occurring Typhlichthys subterraneus by CT-scanned skeletal anatomy and mitochondrial + nuclear phylogenomics; syntopic occurrence despite deep phylogenetic distance is textbook convergent evolution of the cavefish morphotype in a single karst groundwater pool that has been monitored for >30 years; single-cave known range makes D. arcanus among the rarest fishes globally with immediate conservation implications given siting on an active US Army arsenal.

item.title: Episode 36: The H5N1 mutation that isn't what it looked like
item.description: A bioRxiv preprint from Sukhova, Peacock, Barclay and colleagues (Imperial College London) reinterprets the mixed HA-190/226 alleles that appeared in the two severe D1.1 clade-2.3.4.4b human H5N1 cases in Louisiana and British Columbia in late 2024: the mutations do not confer detectable α2,6 sialic-acid (human-upper-airway) receptor usage — the classical pandemic-adaptation switch the field has been watching for — and instead *weaken* α2,3 (avian-type) binding, which correlates with enhanced evasion of the human airway mucosal sialic-acid decoy trap and reduced susceptibility to oseltamivir and zanamivir (looser HA grip lowers dependence on neuraminidase-mediated release); reframes H5 human adaptation as achievable via HA-NA-balance shifts and mucin-escape/antiviral-tolerance rather than the α2,3→α2,6 receptor-switch alone — changing what surveillance sequences should be scored for. A medRxiv preprint from Colizza's group (INSERM/Sorbonne) integrates high-resolution population, air- and land-mobility, geographical accessibility, and conflict-adjusted travel-time data with national health-system readiness to map continental Bundibugyo Ebola importation risk from the ongoing DRC/Uganda PHEIC (3,262 confirmed cases and 1,437 deaths in DRC by 27 July 2026; the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak on record, and one for which no licensed vaccine or therapeutic exists): 85% of continental risk sits in immediate neighbors, with first-tier high risk in South Sudan, Rwanda, Kenya, Tanzania, Zambia, Ethiopia, Burundi, Angola, South Africa, CAR, and Nigeria; largest readiness gaps in South Sudan, Burundi, and CAR; a second tier — Botswana, Burkina Faso, Cameroon, Chad, and Ghana — combines intermediate risk with low readiness and is under-prioritized in current preparedness planning. item.title: Episode 35: How Pseudomonas gets the liver to clear its antibiotics
item.description: A bioRxiv preprint from the Lampe lab (University of Kansas Medical Center) proposes a host-side antibiotic-resistance mechanism for Pseudomonas aeruginosa: its blue-green virulence pigment pyocyanin activates the aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) in human hepatocytes, upregulating CYP1A2 — the P450 that clears fluoroquinolones — and accelerating ciprofloxacin metabolism, so drug concentration reaching the infection drops without any change in the pathogen's own resistance genes. In primary human hepatocytes at 5 µM sub-toxic pyocyanin, CYP1A2 mRNA rose 6.2-fold and oxo-ciprofloxacin metabolite formation rose 3.6-fold; the mechanism reframes AMR as pathogen–host pharmacological warfare and, if it holds in vivo, argues that fully susceptible isolates on a plate can generate sub-therapeutic exposure in patients and select for resistance. On the business side, ProMIS Neurosciences (Nasdaq: PMN; Cambridge, MA / Toronto) reported blinded 6-month interim safety and biomarker data for PMN310 in the Phase 1b PRECISE-AD Alzheimer's trial: 136 patients evaluated at 5, 10, or 20 mg/kg IV, 61% APOE4 carriers and 11% homozygotes; zero cases of ARIA-E and 4.4% ARIA-H (all mild/asymptomatic); no treatment-related SAEs or drug-related discontinuations; 68.5% of patients showed a decline in plasma p-tau217 and 62.5% in CSF MTBR-tau243. PMN310 is a humanized IgG1 selective for toxic soluble amyloid-beta oligomers that avoids plaque and vascular amyloid — mechanistically the target hypothesis is that ARIA is driven by antibody engagement of vascular plaques, and oligomer selectivity could deliver the therapeutic benefit without the vascular disruption that produces 13% (Leqembi) or 24% (Kisunla) ARIA-E rates on approved anti-amyloid antibodies; topline unblinded 12-month readout expected Q1 2027. A bioRxiv preprint from Shoulders and Hie (MIT Chemistry, with Whitney at ANU) applies the ESM-IF1 inverse-folding protein language model to nominate residues in the Nicotiana tabacum Rubisco large subunit for directed evolution, then selects the resulting library in Rubisco-dependent E. coli — recovering multiple improved variants including a single T391I substitution that boosts carboxylation rate 29% and aerobic carboxylation efficiency 43%; several winning substitutions lie outside the plant evolutionary lineage yet remain chloroplast assembly-competent, demonstrating that structure-aware protein language models can propose functional substitutions natural selection never sampled — a template for ML-assisted directed evolution on engineering targets that have resisted classical approaches. The Model Context Protocol (MCP) — the LLM-to-tool wire protocol originated at Anthropic and now governed by the Linux Foundation — finalized its 2026-07-28 specification today: removes the initialize handshake and Mcp-Session-Id header so remote MCP servers can scale on plain round-robin load balancers without sticky sessions or shared session stores; formalizes MCP Apps (sandboxed iframe UIs served by tools) and MCP Tasks (first-class long-running work with tasks/get, tasks/update, tasks/cancel); adds OAuth 2.0/OpenID Connect hardening, W3C Trace Context propagation, JSON Schema 2020-12 support in tool schemas, and a formal deprecation policy — directly relevant for bioinformatics tools, databases, and lab-instrument integrations exposed to AI agents. And a Science paper from McKenzie, Matthews and colleagues (University of British Columbia) shows that Chaoborus edulis phantom-midge larvae in Lake Malawi execute daily 200+ m diel vertical migrations to escape fish predation, using two pairs of resilin-walled air sacs whose volume is controlled by pH-driven changes in the elastic protein rather than active gas exchange; pressure-chamber tests show the sacs withstand pressures corresponding to depths >400 m — twice what the larvae actually experience — reopening the question of why insects have essentially failed to colonize the open ocean.

item.title: Episode 34: How today's H5N1 got a second front door
item.description: A bioRxiv preprint from the Boyd lab (Stanford, with Hensley/Penn) shows that emerging H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b viruses — but not historical H5 lineages — bind human MHC-II HLA-DR and mediate sialic-acid-independent cell entry, identifying a previously unrecognised second receptor pathway distinct from the classical sialic-acid route; HA binding to primary human immune cells scales with MHC-II expression and is modulated by HLA-DR allelic variation (host-genetic susceptibility axis), mammalian-adaptive substitutions in the sialic-acid receptor-binding domain reduce MHC-II binding (implying remodeling of this second mode during human adaptation), and cross-reactive monoclonal antibodies from H5-naïve humans can block the HA–MHC-II interaction — with implications for host range, cellular tropism (MHC-II is on dendritic cells, macrophages, B cells), spillover risk, and therapeutic intervention. On the business side, argenx (Ghent) is acquiring Forte Biosciences for $77/share cash (~$2.2B total, ~86% premium to Forte's VWAP since positive Phase 1b vitiligo data on 9 July 2026) for FB102, a first-in-class anti-CD122 antibody blocking IL-2/IL-15 shared-receptor signaling on pathogenic effector T cells and NK cells while sparing high-affinity CD25-containing Treg receptors; Phase 1b in vitiligo hit statistical significance on the primary endpoint (effect sizes not disclosed in the M&A announcement), Phase 1b in celiac disease was positive last year with Phase 2 in H2 2026, framed as a "pipeline in a product" extending to alopecia areata and other autoimmune indications; funded from cash on hand, closing expected Q3 2026. TriGlue (Li et al., arXiv 2607.22143) formulates molecular-glue-degrader design as a joint ternary-complex generation problem — decomposing into (i) an SE(3)-equivariant protein-protein interface estimator that predicts a geometrically constrained induced interface from unbound E3-ligase and target monomers, then (ii) an interface-conditioned ternary flow-matching network that jointly generates a chemically valid small molecule and the rigid-body transformation assembling the ternary complex; produces valid molecules and plausible ternary complexes across the evaluation suite and is one of the first attempts to co-model glue chemistry, induced PPI interface, and rigid-body assembly under proper geometric-symmetry constraints — an architectural template for degrader-chemistry generative models. Moonshot AI released open weights for Kimi K3 on Hugging Face on 26 July 2026 under a modified MIT license: a 2.8-trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 16-of-896 experts active per token, 1M-token context, ~1.4TB compressed; per Moonshot's own numbers behind Claude Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol on aggregate but ahead of Claude Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.5 on coding/agentic benchmarks; largest open-weight release ever — directly relevant for on-prem biomedical/clinical/HIPAA-constrained deployments where frontier closed APIs can't be used. And a Science paper from Al-Ashqar & Sallam (Mansoura University Vertebrate Paleontology Center) with Seiffert (USC) describes Masripithecus moghraensis, a new ~17–18 Ma Early Miocene ape from a lower-jaw fragment recovered at Wadi Moghra, northern Egypt (2023–2024 fieldwork); morphology places it closer to living apes than any known East African contemporary, arguing that deep ape ancestry may sit in a North Africa / Middle East forested-Tethys-margin corridor rather than a single East African cradle.

item.title: Episode 33: How a transcription error helps flu dodge antibodies
item.description: A bioRxiv preprint from Sanchez-Ruiz and colleagues (University of Granada) maps the per-site transcription-error landscape of influenza hemagglutinin (HA) mRNA using consensus high-throughput sequencing and finds that the single most prevalent error encodes a phenotypic (non-heritable) amino-acid replacement that impairs binding of broadly neutralising antibodies. The site mistranslates at ~0.2–0.5% per translation event, so a stable subpopulation of every infection displays antibody-escape HA on real virions without any genomic mutation — a "programmed-recoding"-like escape axis invisible to sequencing, which may partially explain why bnAb neutralisation titres don't translate cleanly to real-world protection. On the business side, the FDA Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee on 23 July 2026 narrowly voted to add BPC-157 (ulcerative colitis), KPV, TB-500 (both wound healing) and MOTS-c (weight loss) to the 503A Bulks List despite FDA reviewers recommending against — all four had been banned three years earlier over safety concerns and none has substantive human efficacy/safety data; the mechanism to relegitimise wellness peptides is the compounding-pharmacy pathway rather than the drug-approval pipeline (three more peptides — Emideltide, Semax, Epitalon — vote later in the week). Sanofi on 24 July 2026 discontinued OX40L-targeting amlitelimab in atopic dermatitis after inconsistent Phase-3 efficacy and Kaposi's-sarcoma cases (a signal also seen with the competing Amgen/Kyowa Kirin OX40L programme), leaving the mechanism itself under a cloud and Sanofi facing a widening post-Dupixent gap. An arXiv paper from Jiatong Li et al. shows that chemical chain-of-thought reasoning in LLMs is a "hallucination-prone molecular scratchpad": intermediate reasoning steps contain widespread fabricated substructures/atoms even when final answers are correct, but perturbing that scratchpad changes the final answer — so the trace is causally load-bearing yet unfaithful, and reading the chain-of-thought is not a valid way to verify LLM chemistry output. And a Science Advances paper from Krabbenhoft's group (University at Buffalo / USGS) uses long-read sequencing on Guam brown tree snakes and finds >19,000 structural variants affecting ~8× more of the genome than SNVs, enriched in immunity and olfactory-receptor genes — providing a genomic explanation for how a founder-population of a few snakes reached >30,000/mi² and rewriting the "essentially clonal" short-read narrative for this and probably other post-bottleneck invasive/endangered populations.
item.itunes:summary: Influenza-hemagglutinin phenotypic mutation as antibody escape (Sanchez-Ruiz et al., University of Granada, bioRxiv 2026-07-25): consensus high-throughput sequencing maps per-site transcription-error rates on HA mRNA; the top-ranked error encodes a phenotypic amino-acid replacement that impairs binding of broadly neutralising antibodies; mistranslation at ~0.2–0.5% means a stable low-frequency subpopulation of every infection displays escape HA on real virions with no genomic change — programmed-recoding-analogous escape axis invisible to genome sequencing; plausible partial explanation for the neutralisation-titre-to-real-world-protection gap for bnAb-based universal flu vaccines. item.title: Episode 32: The math on Ebola travel screening
item.description: A medRxiv preprint from Quilty and colleagues (Charité — Universitätsmedizin Berlin, with the CMMID Bundibugyo Working Group) uses a stochastic simulation model to estimate airport syndromic-screening effectiveness for the ongoing 2026 Bundibugyo ebolavirus PHEIC in DRC/Uganda: for a 12-hour international flight at 86% screening sensitivity, ~73% of infected travellers evade combined exit + entry screening (95% CrI 68–77%), and 92% of those who board arrive undetected; even in a conservative all-cases-febrile scenario the undetected fraction is ~64%; the mechanistic reading is that Bundibugyo's ~7.7-day incubation and ~4-day onset-to-severe interval leave almost no room for symptom-based detection, so meaningful control has to come from source-country outbreak response, receiving-country clinical surveillance, and post-departure self-monitoring. The FDA on 24 July 2026 approved Otsuka's Simtriyo (centanafadine) for ADHD in adults and pediatrics ages 6+ (≥20 kg): first-in-class norepinephrine-dopamine-serotonin reuptake inhibitor (NDSRI) — adding serotonin reuptake to the classical norepinephrine-plus-dopamine ADHD pharmacology — supported by four Phase 3 trials (2 adult, 1 adolescent, 1 pediatric) with statistically significant improvements on ADHD-RS-5 and AISRS vs placebo, plus a Phase 3b in adults with comorbid anxiety showing placebo separation by week 1; a genuinely new pharmacological class for ADHD and a plausible option for patients with comorbid mood/anxiety symptoms. A bioRxiv preprint from Lal, Yang, Zhang and Arnold (Caltech) applies active-learning-assisted directed evolution (ALDE) to a promiscuous protoglobin parent enzyme across 26 carbene/nitrene transfer reactions: every reaction the parent already catalysed was improved by at least one ALDE variant, and — more strikingly — ALDE-designed variants catalysed 5 of 10 reactions the parent could not perform at all; the significance is a template for compact one-library-many-activities enzyme libraries that compress the front end of biocatalyst discovery. Anthropic on 24 July 2026 released Claude Opus 5: half the cost of Fable 5 ($5/M input, $25/M output; identical to Opus 4.8) with ~Fable-5-level intelligence, 1M-token context, 128K synchronous output, a new 5-level effort control, ~79% SWE-bench Pro, ~3× next-best on ARC-AGI-3, lowest misaligned-behaviour score of any recent Claude, and substantially reduced classifier over-refusal — directly relevant for biomedical/clinical/agentic workloads that touch dual-use topics. A PeerJ paper from Noda and colleagues (Kyoto University) uses micro-CT and geometric morphometrics on three fossil vertebrae collected 1995–1997 from the Tsubusagawa Formation on Kyushu to erect Limnospondylus ajimuensis, a new cryptobranchid giant salamander (~1.1 m) from ~3.5 Ma freshwater lake sediments — evidence that the Cryptobranchidae family used to occupy lake habitats and not only fast-flowing rivers, with the lake-adapted lineages going extinct around Pliocene–Pleistocene cooling.

item.title: Episode 31: The evolutionary ceiling on dairy H5N1
item.description: A bioRxiv preprint from Machkovech, Friedrich, Kawaoka and colleagues (Wisconsin) deep-sequences ferret infections and ferret-to-ferret transmission events with two bovine-derived H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b B3.13 genotype viruses: within-host viral genetic diversity was limited with weak purifying selection and no signal of mammalian adaptation (no PB2, HA receptor-binding, or fusion-pH sweep), and airborne transmission — when it happened — proceeded through stringent bottlenecks that randomize which within-host variants get through; the mechanistic reading is an evolutionary ceiling on acute-infection adaptation that helps explain why efficient replication in ferrets has not translated to efficient transmission, while emphasising continued deep-sequencing surveillance of the dairy outbreak because rare bottleneck breakthroughs remain possible. A bioRxiv preprint from He, Cao and colleagues (Peking University) characterises SARS-CoV-2 sublineages PQ.16.1.1 and RK.1, both descendants of NB.1.8.1 dominating the Asia-Pacific and each independently carrying the RBD mutation D420N: surface plasmon resonance and pseudovirus assays show reduced ACE2 engagement offset by profound escape from Class 1 neutralising monoclonal antibodies and Wuhan-Hu-1-primed convalescent plasma — a classical receptor-binding/immune-escape trade-off surfacing via convergent evolution, arguing for updated vaccine antigens covering the D420N background. The FDA on 22 July 2026 approved GSK's Jideytro (zidesamtinib) for adults with locally advanced or metastatic ROS1-positive NSCLC previously treated with a ROS1 kinase inhibitor: selective ROS1 TKI engineered to retain potency against the G2032R resistance mutant and to penetrate the blood-brain barrier; ARROS-1 Phase 1/2 in 117 previously-treated patients showed 44% ORR (95% CI 34–53%) with 6-month DoR 82% and 12-month 69%; Breakthrough Therapy + Orphan Drug designations, approved ~8 weeks ahead of PDUFA target; first approved medicine from GSK's recently closed $10.6B Nuvalent acquisition and GSK's first lung-cancer drug, with a next-generation ALK inhibitor following the same playbook. A bioRxiv preprint from Zhang, Ning and colleagues (Huazhong University of Science and Technology) introduces MGM2, a multimodal microbiome foundation model pretrained on 1,821,291 MicrobeAtlas samples and 225,067 OTUs at 99% clustering that couples NTv3-derived microbial sequence embeddings with abundance conditioning and community-semantic alignment: frozen MGM2 representations beat DeepPhylo by 0.06–0.21 macro-AUROC across five held-out MGnify hierarchy levels, MGM2-XLarge hits 0.79 AUROC for fecal microbiota transplantation response and 15% Bray-Curtis reduction post-transplant vs recipient baseline, and supports ASV-level trend forecasting across 24 wastewater treatment plants; sparse-autoencoder analysis resolves representations into 4,096 features spanning taxonomy, abundance state, ecological context and technical variation — pushing microbiome analysis beyond cohort-specific abundance tables toward transferable learned representations. A Frontiers in Ethology paper from Ayres (Beneath the Waves) and colleagues describes "ram-to-fragment" predation by orcas (Orcinus orca) on sharp-tail sunfish (Masturus lanceolatus) in the Gulf of California: two documented events (July 2024 and September 2025), in which one adult holds the sunfish by the tail fin and a second adult strikes it head-on at high speed, fragmenting the tough, gelatinous carcass into pieces the juvenile can consume; interpretive options include mechanical portioning for calf provisioning, microbiome-related nutritional benefit, or social play — a hunting strategy not previously formally described in orcas.

item.title: Episode 30: An artemisinin-resistance mutation reaches Somalia
item.description: A medRxiv preprint from Arale et al. (Mogadishu / WHO / King's College London) reports the first confirmed detection of the validated artemisinin partial-resistance marker pfkelch13 R622I in Somalia, from a P. falciparum infection collected in Dolow, Gedo region — closing a long-standing surveillance gap between R622I-endemic Ethiopia/Eritrea/Sudan; the same 2023 nationwide dried-blood-spot survey (n≈7,100) also characterises pfhrp2 deletions at ~4% (95% CI overlapping WHO's 5% RDT-switch threshold) and pfhrp3 deletions at ~37%, meaning diagnostic redundancy is already compromised. A medRxiv preprint from da Silva et al. (Andrews lab, Stanford, with Nepali collaborators) sequences 350 S. Typhi and 114 S. Paratyphi A isolates collected 2018–2024 alongside ~1,800 previously published Nepal genomes to evaluate the impact of the April 2022 nationwide typhoid conjugate vaccine (TCV) rollout: S. Typhi H58 contracted sharply during the pandemic, lineage 3.3 contracted specifically post-TCV, S. Paratyphi A (not vaccine-targeted) showed only mild pandemic-era decline; no evidence of vaccine escape at the Vi capsule; fluoroquinolone non-susceptibility now ~70.6% (S. Typhi) and 99.1% (S. Paratyphi A), arguing for bivalent Typhi–Paratyphi conjugate vaccines. Agios Pharmaceuticals on 21 July 2026 discontinued its next-generation pyruvate kinase activator tebapivat in sickle cell disease after a placebo-controlled Phase 2 (n=59) failed to establish differentiation: hemoglobin response rates 43.8%/47.1%/29.4% across the 2.5/5.0/7.5 mg once-daily arms vs 33.3% placebo — no consistent dose response, safety unchanged from prior SCD experience; strategic focus shifts to mitapivat (sNDA under FDA priority review, PDUFA target 1 Nov 2026). Anthropic on 21 July 2026 announced a Rare Disease Research Claude Grants program offering up to $50,000 in Claude credits over six months across basic-research and biotech tracks (applications open through 2 August); named partners include the Monarch Initiative (Mondo Disease Ontology + Monarch Knowledge Graph, plus the new DisMech mechanistic-similarity library), Every Cure (drug-repurposing search), the Centre for Population Genomics (variant classification for undiagnosed patients), and Violet Research Institute (regulatory workflows) — positioning Claude as a reasoning layer on top of curated biomedical ontologies rather than a wet-lab operation. A PNAS paper from Beye and colleagues (Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf, with Cologne and Frankfurt collaborators, published 20 July 2026) identifies a specific set of doublesex-expressing neurons in the honeybee brain that implements age-based polyethism: conditional silencing of these neurons in older worker bees reverts them to nurse/queen-attending behavior; restoring activity restores age-appropriate foraging behavior — a clean gene-to-circuit-to-behavior-to-colony-level mapping in a canonical self-organizing biological system, with implications for other insects that share the deeply conserved doublesex gene.

item.title: Episode 29: The flu that broke the flu assay
item.description: A bioRxiv preprint from Liang et al. (Utrecht University; de Vries and Fouchier labs) reports that H3N2 influenza A subclade K (J.2.4.1) — the dominant Northern Hemisphere strain in the 2025–2026 season — has lost the ability to agglutinate turkey erythrocytes: hemagglutinin substitutions at positions 140, 192, and 223 near the receptor-binding site shift binding preference toward elongated glycans not displayed on turkey red blood cells; glycan array, ELISA, flow cytometry, and hemagglutination-inhibition assays confirm the shift; computational modeling shows F192 forms a stabilizing CH–Pi interaction with elongated glycan; because the WHO's HAI assay for antigenic characterization and vaccine strain selection depends on turkey erythrocyte agglutination, subclade K is effectively invisible to the standard assay; the authors show glyco-remodeled erythrocytes (previously developed by the same group) restore assay signal for subclade K and could support ongoing surveillance and vaccine development. A medRxiv preprint from da Fonseca et al. (Walter lab, University of Utah) reports the first large genomic population-structure analysis of Coccidioides in the United States: 312 whole-genome sequences (186 prospectively collected from a national diagnostic lab, 126 previously published) — 139 C. immitis, 173 C. posadasii — reveal three major populations per species (C. immitis: two California-centered plus a Pacific Northwest population; C. posadasii: two Arizona-centered plus a Texas-centered population); MRCAs ~127,000 y (C. immitis) and ~234,000 y (C. posadasii); ancestral-area reconstruction shows asymmetric outward dispersal from California and from Arizona/Texas; most populations biallelic for mating type (sexual recombination) but one C. immitis population and a Brazilian C. posadasii subgroup are clonal; all populations show recent demographic expansion, supporting expanded genomic surveillance to detect Valley-fever range shifts as climate changes. Bristol Myers Squibb announced on July 20 the purchase of an NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD built on the new Vera Rubin architecture — the first Vera Rubin SuperPOD purchase by a life-sciences company: ~10× compute per watt vs Blackwell generation; will host BMS-proprietary foundation models on internal small-molecule, biologics, and clinical data plus agentic drug-discovery workflows across oncology, hematology, cardiovascular, immunology, and neuroscience; CRO cites a sickle-cell disease asset in the pipeline as AI-enabled, and points to a shift from ~10 to dozens of candidates evaluated early in each program; financial terms not disclosed. A paper in Palaeontology from Silva Júnior et al. (São Paulo State University / Tübingen) uses finite element analysis on femur reconstructions of two Late Cretaceous South American titanosaurs — Uberabatitan ribeiroi (Brazil) and Neuquensaurus australis (Argentina) — under simulated gravity and muscle loading during bipedal rearing: unusually robust femur cross-sections distribute stress well enough for juvenile individuals to have reared up, but scaling of body mass with growth exceeds bone's ability to distribute stress, so fully grown adults likely could not.
item.itunes:summary: H3N2 subclade K loses hemagglutination (Liang et al., Utrecht, bioRxiv 2026-07-20): the dominant 2025/26 Northern Hemisphere H3N2 lineage acquires HA substitutions at positions 140/192/223 near the receptor-binding site, shifting binding preference toward elongated glycans not displayed on turkey erythrocytes; standard WHO hemagglutination-inhibition assay for antigenic characterization and vaccine strain selection therefore fails or gives noisy results for subclade K; glyco-remodeled erythrocytes engineered to display elongated glycans restore assay signal. item.title: Episode 28: H5N1 Finds a Silent Route into Pigs
item.description: A bioRxiv preprint from Ohio State University (Liu et al.) directly inoculates lactating sows via the intramammary route with bovine H5N1 virus to test susceptibility in commercially vaccinated swine: all inoculated sows developed productive infection confirmed by sustained viral RNA shedding in milk, mammary gland lesions, viral antigen staining, and seroconversion, despite prior swine influenza vaccination; none showed overt clinical disease or respiratory involvement; suckling piglets showed intermittent oral viral RNA tracking milk viral kinetics; establishes that commercial swine are susceptible to bovine H5N1 via a milk/mammary route and that subclinical infection invisible to standard surveillance is the likely outcome, underscoring the need to extend H5N1 surveillance to swine given the species' role as a reassortment mixing vessel. A bioRxiv preprint from Mukherjee et al. (Indiana) uses 18-month stepwise dihydroartemisinin pressure on a 2018 artemisinin-sensitive Chittagong Hill Tracts P. falciparum clone (27 cycles to 1600 nM) to generate three independently evolved resistant lines; all three convergently acquired distinct loss-of-function mutations in pfkic1 (PF3D7_0606000), encoding KIC1, a protein in the Kelch13-associated endocytic compartment; targeted pfkic1 disruption in the parental clone elevated ring-stage survival and accelerated post-drug recovery, functionally validating KIC1; in 22 CHT field isolates all carrying wild-type pfkelch13, natural pfkic1 variation was associated with ring-stage survival and parasite clearance in patients — a Kelch13-independent artemisinin resistance pathway invisible to standard pfkelch13 surveillance. GSK announced discontinuation of camlipixant, a P2X3 receptor antagonist, for refractory chronic cough after mixed Phase 3 results: CALM-1 met its primary endpoint (50 mg BID, week-12 cough frequency reduction vs placebo) but CALM-2 (24-week) did not reach statistical significance with the same dose; 25 mg BID failed in both trials; key secondary patient-reported outcomes including the Chronic Cough Diary score did not meet thresholds in either study; GSK will discontinue the cough program and focus camlipixant development in irritable bowel syndrome. A paper in the Journal of Paleontology from Churchill et al. (UNSW) describes three new marsupial species from Riversleigh Early Miocene deposits (~18 Mya) in northwestern Queensland and proposes a sixth marsupial order, Keeunamorphia, with Gondwanan origins greater than 50 million years ago that persisted in Australia for roughly 35 million years before disappearing in the Middle Miocene ~12 Mya.
item.itunes:summary: H5N1 bovine-swine mammary transmission (Liu et al., Ohio State, bioRxiv 2026-07-18): intramammary inoculation of commercially vaccinated lactating sows with bovine H5N1; productive infection confirmed by sustained viral RNA shedding in milk, mammary lesions, antigen staining, seroconversion; no clinical disease or respiratory signs; piglet oral swabs positive intermittently tracking milk virus; vaccination did not prevent infection; establishes subclinical swine susceptibility via milk/mammary route; calls for expanded swine H5N1 surveillance given species' role as reassortment mixing vessel. KIC1 as Kelch13-independent artemisinin resistance determinant in Bangladesh P. falciparum (Nima et al., Indiana, bioRxiv 2026-07-17): 18-month stepwise DHA pressure on wild-type-kelch13 Chittagong clone; three independent lines converge on pfkic1 loss-of-function (stop-gain or frameshift); disrupts Kelch13-associated endocytic compartment reducing heme-driven artemisinin activation; 7-11-fold RSA survival increase vs parental; targeted pfkic1 disruption validates causality; 22 CHT field isolates -- pfkic1 variation associated with RSA survival and parasite clearance (PC50); mechanism invisible to standard pfkelch13 surveillance. GSK camlipixant (P2X3 antagonist, $2B deal) discontinued for refractory chronic cough: CALM-1 positive (50 mg BID, 12-wk cough frequency); CALM-2 (24-wk) missed primary endpoint same dose; 25 mg both fail; CCD secondary outcomes below threshold both studies; P2X3 mechanism validated by MSD's gefapixant approval; camlipixant will continue in IBS-D/IBS-M (BALANCE trial). Keeunamorphia: new sixth marsupial order (Churchill et al., UNSW, Journal of Paleontology, July 2026): Riversleigh Miocene deposits (~18 Mya); three new species 25-200g; dental morphology geometrically distinct from all five existing orders; divergence >50 Mya (Gondwanan origin); lineage persisted ~35 Myr, disappeared Middle Miocene ~12 Mya.

item.title: Episode 27: The toxin dying bacteria leave behind
item.description: A bioRxiv preprint from a large UK multicenter team (Glasgow, Liverpool, London, Netherlands) identifies histone-like proteins — bacterial DNA-binding proteins released from dying meningococci when killed by antibiotics — as the drivers of vascular barrier failure in meningococcal sepsis: treating primary human endothelial cells with ceftriaxone-lysed N. meningitidis causes VE-cadherin disruption and EPCR shedding within three hours via histone-like proteins, not LPS (an LPS-null strain shows identical barrier collapse to wild-type), confirmed in patient skin biopsies where histone-like proteins co-localize with fibrinogen-leak zones at purpuric lesion edges; non-anticoagulant heparins and anti-HLP antibody cocktails reverse the damage, pointing to co-administration at the moment of first antibiotic dose as the therapeutic strategy, with conservation of the mechanism across streptococcal and staphylococcal bacteria extending potential clinical reach. A team from Oregon Health and Science University, Portland, and the Galveston National Laboratory posted the first mRNA-lipid nanoparticle vaccine evaluation against Neisseria gonorrhoeae — the bacterium responsible for 82 million annual gonorrhea cases and a WHO priority resistant pathogen — delivering a BamA outer membrane antigen that raises strong systemic and mucosal antibodies recognizing diverse clinical isolates including ceftriaxone-resistant strains; neither intramuscular nor intranasal delivery accelerated bacterial clearance in a mouse vaginal infection model and there was no serum bactericidal activity, establishing the first mRNA vaccine trial against any gram-negative bacterium and defining the gap: gonorrhea's sophisticated immune evasion neutralizes complement even when antibodies are generated. A team from the Pontificia Universidad Católica de Chile published in The Lancet Microbe the first nationwide full-genome characterization of Andes virus from human clinical samples — 58 patients 2011–2024, whole-genome sequencing across all three RNA segments — identifying two lineages (Chi-North in central Chile, ANDV-South in southern Chile) with no geographic mixing; critically, sequences from four patients with confirmed person-to-person transmission showed no consistent genetic signatures distinguishing them from sporadic cases, meaning genomic surveillance cannot predict which infections will seed human-to-human spread, with direct relevance to the April–July 2026 M.V. Hondius cruise ship outbreak (13 cases, 3 deaths) declared over July 2. And a University of Sydney and Texas A&M team in Molecular Biology and Evolution calculates the first de novo koala mutation rate from hundreds of genomes and reconstructs population history: a near-extinction bottleneck beginning roughly 100,000 years ago bottomed around 60,000 years ago — 45,000 years before the first humans arrived in Australia — caused by eucalyptus loss during the last glacial maximum; the five east-coast populations diverged 16,500–6,000 years ago, and the low genetic diversity of modern koalas reflects that ancient founding event, not solely European-era hunting.
item.itunes:summary: Meningococcal HLPs drive purpura fulminans (UK multicenter, bioRxiv 2026-07-16): ceftriaxone-killed N. meningitidis releases histone-like proteins (hupB, IHFα, IHFβ); electrical impedance assay shows endothelial barrier collapse within 3h via VE-cadherin disruption and EPCR shedding; LPS-null strain shows identical barrier collapse — LPS drives ICAM-1 upregulation but not barrier breach; recombinant HLPs dose-dependently toxic; HLPs confirmed in extracellular space of patient skin biopsies co-localizing with fibrinogen-leak zones; streptococcal and staphylococcal HLPs also toxic (mechanism conserved across gram-positives); non-anticoagulant heparins and anti-HLP antibody cocktails reverse damage in vitro and in Galleria mellonella model; clinical implication — co-administer HLP neutralizer with first ceftriaxone dose. BamA mRNA-LNP gonorrhea vaccine (Sikora et al., OHSU/Portland/Galveston, bioRxiv 2026-07-16): first mRNA-LNP vaccine against any gram-negative bacterium; BamA outer membrane protein, IM or IN delivery in mice; strong systemic and mucosal (vaginal wash) anti-BamA IgG recognizing diverse clinical isolates including ceftriaxone-resistant strains; NO accelerated bacterial clearance in murine vaginal infection model; NO serum bactericidal activity; gonorrhea immune evasion neutralizes complement downstream of antigen binding; next steps — different antigens, complement-fixing adjuvants, mucosal delivery optimization. Andes virus nationwide genomics, Chile (PUC Chile, Lancet Microbe, 2026-07-15): 58 human clinical cases 2011–2024, whole S/M/L segment sequencing; two lineages — Chi-North (central Chile) and ANDV-South (southern Chile) — geographically segregated, no mixing; four P2P-transmission-confirmed case sequences show no consistent genetic signatures vs sporadic cases — capacity for human-to-human spread not readable from genome; both lineages carry distinct glycoprotein amino acid profiles (vaccine-design implication); context: MV Hondius cruise ship outbreak April–July 2026, 13 cases, 3 deaths, declared over July 2. Koala glacial bottleneck (U. Sydney/Texas A&M, Mol Biol Evol, 2026-07-15): first de novo koala mutation rate calculated from hundreds of genomes; population collapse began ~100,000 ya, bottomed ~60,000 ya (last glacial maximum, eucalyptus loss); 45,000 years before first humans arrived ~55,000 ya; five east-coast populations radiated 16,500–6,000 ya; low genetic diversity of modern koalas explained by ancient founding event, not solely European-era hunting; species survived a worse bottleneck before — conservation resilience precedent.

item.title: Episode 26: The Ebola numbers that aren't what they seem
item.description: A medRxiv preprint from Bouhentala and Kadir at Mohamed Khider University in Biskra takes the same public WHO surveillance data on the 2026 DRC Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak that daily briefings quote and argues the recent 18-day plateau in confirmed cases (40–52/day from 25 June to 13 July) is not transmission control but saturated case detection — the death-to-case ratio inside each reporting interval rose from 0.28 to 0.58 over the same window, a pattern only consistent with a diagnostic ceiling; Richardson-Lucy deconvolution of onset dates puts the true doubling time at ~90 days rather than the 22 days computed from cumulative counts, Rt at 1.28 (95% CrI 1.15–1.41) on 7 July, and outcome-delay-adjusted CFR at 50.2% (67.3% resolved-case) vs the crude 37.5%, with provincial CFR reaching 81% in newly affected provinces. A Labcorp team posted the first US-wide integrated mpox genomic surveillance program (medRxiv 2026-07-17): 326 whole genomes from residual clinical specimens across all 10 HHS regions using Molecular Loop probe capture + PacBio Sequel II long-read sequencing, detecting two Clade Ib introductions (January and June 2025), 13 Clade IIb lineages, large 1.6–17.6 kb inverted-terminal-repeat deletions, and APOBEC3 mutation signatures confirming ongoing human-to-human transmission in both clades — the SARS-CoV-2 sequencing infrastructure now doing double-duty for orthopoxvirus surveillance. The FDA on 16 July 2026 granted traditional approval to Novartis's Fabhalta (iptacopan) for slowing kidney function decline in adults with primary IgA nephropathy — the first and only complement inhibitor ever approved with a kidney-protection endpoint in IgAN; the oral factor B inhibitor shuts off the alternative-pathway C3 convertase amplification loop, and in Phase 3 APPLAUSE-IgAN slowed eGFR decline by 48% (–3.0 vs –5.7 mL/min/1.73m²/yr) on top of standard RAS-blockade, with a REMS program mandating meningococcal vaccination. Google DeepMind and Isomorphic Labs on 16 July 2026 formally launched a joint bioresilience program organized as Prevent/Detect/Respond — extending SynthID watermarking to synthetic biological sequences, deploying AlphaEvolve to optimize metagenomic sequencing pipelines, and standing up an Isomorphic Labs medical-countermeasures unit built on the IsoDDE drug-design engine, with 15+ government/biosecurity partnerships already in place; the framing positions AlphaFold, AlphaGenome, and IsoDDE as biosecurity infrastructure rather than pure drug-discovery tools. Gemini 3.5 Pro missed a third launch deadline as of 16 July with the rebuilt base model still hitting hallucination/consistency issues and the trade press now floating a "stopgap release"; separately, the NYT reported on 17 July that Meta is in talks to lease compute capacity to Anthropic in a deal worth up to $10B over two years — mirroring Anthropic's May compute deal with SpaceX and signaling that top-tier training demand is now outrunning the traditional AWS/Azure/GCP triangle. And a Christian Hellmich-led paper in Biophysics Reviews (TU Wien + University of Vienna, published 14 July 2026) shows the jaws of the Mediterranean bristle worm Perinereis cultrifera behave mechanically like a metal — displaying the Nix-Gao nanoindentation size effect characteristic of crystalline copper and silver — but with size-dependent elasticity that distinguishes them from any true metal, proposing a new material category called "bio-metals" defined by protein scaffolds studded with individual metal ions (likely zinc) concentrated at the jaw tip.

item.title: Episode 25: The pill that unseats the cholesterol shots
item.description: The FDA on 16 July 2026 approved Merck's Lipfendra (enlicitide) as the first once-daily oral PCSK9 inhibitor for adults with hypercholesterolemia — a macrocyclic peptide big enough to span the PCSK9/LDL-receptor protein-protein interface but small and rigid enough to be absorbed as a 20 mg tablet, delivering ~56% LDL-C reduction vs placebo in the Phase 3 CORALreef Lipids trial (n=2,904) and ~59% in CORALreef HeFH (n=303), essentially matching the injectable antibodies Repatha and Praluent that have been the gold standard for a decade; a cardiovascular outcomes trial is still ongoing. The WHO's latest Disease Outbreak News on the DRC Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak puts it at ~2,000 confirmed cases and 700+ deaths across five provinces with the virus now in Haut-Uele and Tshopo beyond the Ituri epicenter, and 80% of new cases coming from unknown chains of transmission outside the contact-tracing net — WHO's Chikwe Ihekweazu called it the fastest-growing single-month expansion of any Ebola outbreak the agency has ever managed, a threshold at which contact tracing alone can no longer contain the outbreak. A Julian Rayner-lab bioRxiv preprint (Cambridge/Colombia) uses AlphaFold-based structural homology to the human lysosomal transporter SLC38A9 to map South-American-specific PfAAT1 mutations onto the transporter's substrate channel, and CRISPR-Cas9 reversion of the V231D mutation in the 7G8 strain significantly reduces chloroquine resistance — the first functional evidence that a distinct South American PfAAT1 mutation set modulates chloroquine resistance, arguing that global molecular surveillance calibrated only to African and Asian mutations undercounts New-World resistance. Eli Lilly announced a definitive agreement to acquire AtaiBeckley — the merged atai Life Sciences/Beckley Psytech entity — for ~$2.8B upfront + up to $1B in CVRs (~$3.8B total, $6.75/share + $2.50 CVR), the first big-pharma acquisition of a pure-play psychedelic depression developer; lead asset BPL-003 is intranasal 5-MeO-DMT, a short-acting 5-HT2A agonist that in a 193-patient Phase 2b delivered 11–12-point MADRS reductions vs 5.8 for low-dose active control after a single 8 or 12 mg dose with effect sustained through 8 weeks and 63% response / 48% remission in the open-label extension. A São Paulo team (Hospital Israelita Albert Einstein) posted the first independent large-scale benchmark of the Evo 2 20B genomic foundation model on ~19,400 RefSeq viral genomes — embeddings hit 0.96 accuracy on Baltimore class and 0.99 on host domain and encode gene density, coding fraction, and gene overlap (R = 0.61–0.77) far beyond a 6-mer composition baseline (0.10–0.38), but generative perplexity is 1.18 bits/nt for bacteriophages vs 1.80 for held-out eukaryote-infecting viruses, meaning generative fidelity is a strong function of training exposure and should not be assumed for novel viral families; a natural counterpoint to Ep 21's Goodfire/Mayo Evo 2 human-variant work. And a Yale/Lukuru Wildlife Research Foundation team publishing in PLOS One on 15 July 2026 describes Colobus congoensis ("Likweli"), a new species of black-coated, orange-lipped colobus monkey from Lomami National Park in eastern DRC — the fifth new African monkey species in 75 years, whose 4.7–5.8 Mya divergence from Colobus satanas is the deepest split in the Colobus genus, older than the human-chimp split.

item.title: Episode 24: The plant virus that fixes wastewater sequencing
item.description: A Pardis Sabeti-led medRxiv preprint retrospectively evaluates seven normalization strategies for wastewater metagenomic sequencing across 1,425 samples from 25 US sites (CASPER consortium), and finds that normalizing by tobamovirus reads — the genus of diet-derived plant viruses that ride through the human gut, of which pepper mild mottle virus is the PCR gold-standard — improves clinical concordance in 18 of 19 pathogen-and-comparison combinations, with the biggest gains for year-round SARS-CoV-2 and norovirus and median gains roughly five times larger than median losses; the practical implication is that a single pathogen-agnostic metagenomic sample can now deliver quantitative trends comparable to targeted wastewater PCR while retaining the ability to detect unknown pathogens. A structural biology preprint solves the first crystal structure of rifamycin B and its complex with bacterial RNA polymerase and shows that its distinctive C-4 O-carboxymethyl substituent forms a salt bridge with fork loop 2 of the RNAP β-subunit that isn't made by clinical rifampicin, giving rifamycin B partial retention of inhibitory activity against S531-type rifampicin-resistance mutations — a proof of principle that the seventy-year-untouched C-4 position on the rifamycin scaffold is a design handle for new drugs that hold up against multidrug-resistant TB. The FDA on 14 July 2026 approved Celcuity's Revtorpyk (gedatolisib) — the first and only pan-class-I-PI3K (α/β/δ/γ) plus mTORC1/2 inhibitor — in combination with palbociclib and fulvestrant for HR+/HER2-, PIK3CA-wildtype advanced or metastatic breast cancer after progression on endocrine therapy, on the strength of a Phase 3 VIKTORIA-1 triplet PFS of 9.3 vs 2.0 months (HR 0.24) and ORR 32% vs 1%; a PIK3CA-mutant supplemental filing is planned for Q3. Chai Discovery closed a $400M Series C at a $3.8B valuation (Index Ventures lead, tripling from seven months earlier), significant less for the raise than for the customer list — antibody design workflows now running at Lilly, Pfizer, and Novartis, three top-ten pharmas whose internal AI teams don't buy outside inference unless it's demonstrably better. And a Frontiers in Psychology study from Juan Manuel García-Ruiz's group at the Donostia International Physics Center in Spain shows that chimpanzees at the Rainfer Foundation strongly prefer quartz and calcite crystals over ordinary pebbles, hold them to eye level and rotate them, and can spot small crystals among 20 pebbles within seconds — arguing that the human fascination with transparent geometric stones predates our species by at least six million years.
item.itunes:summary: Sabeti-lab wastewater metagenomics normalization (Justen et al., medRxiv 2026-07-14): 1,425 CASPER-consortium samples across 25 US sites; tobamovirus-genus normalization improves clinical concordance in 18/19 pathogen-source combinations; median gains ~5x median losses; largest gains for year-round SARS-CoV-2 and norovirus, smaller for sharply seasonal flu/RSV where baseline was already high; brings WW-MGS to targeted-PCR-comparable quantitative accuracy while retaining pathogen-agnostic detection — the surveillance holy grail. item.title: Episode 23: The noise that saves malaria parasites
item.description: A Spielmann-lab bioRxiv preprint uses paired isogenic Plasmodium falciparum lines (wild-type K13 vs C580Y) and single-cell Kelch13 protein quantification to show that survival of artemisinin in genetically resistant parasites is governed by stochastic cell-to-cell variation in Kelch13 abundance rather than by the mutation alone — low-Kelch13 parasites survive because Kelch13 mediates hemoglobin uptake and hence heme-driven artemisinin activation, high-Kelch13 parasites die, and each resistance mutation reshapes the population distribution rather than dictating a fixed phenotype, with low-Kelch13 states carrying a fitness cost via prolonged cell cycle — a paradigm-shifting explanation for partial artemisinin efficacy in fully mutated populations and a suggestion that pushing Kelch13 up could re-sensitize resistant parasites without new chemistry. At AAIC 2026 in London, Biogen and Ionis presented Phase 2 CELIA data on diranersen (BIIB080), a tau-mRNA-targeting antisense oligonucleotide, in 416 patients with early Alzheimer's disease across three intrathecal dose regimens over 18 months: the trial technically missed its primary endpoint (dose-response on CDR-SB) — the best clinical effect was seen at the lowest dose (60 mg Q6M), which slowed CDR-SB by 26%, ADAS-Cog13 by 42%, MMSE by 50%, and modified iADRS by 30% vs placebo, comparable magnitude to the anti-amyloid antibodies, with 50–65% reduction in CSF total tau and PET-tau decreases across every brain region and every dose; Biogen is advancing diranersen to Phase 3 — arguably the first credible anti-tau positive cognitive signal in an Alzheimer's randomized trial. AstraZeneca inked a licensing deal with Dizal Pharmaceuticals for ex-China global rights to Zegfrovy (sunvozertinib), an oral irreversible EGFR TKI approved in China and the US for EGFR exon 20 insertion NSCLC post-chemotherapy — $600M upfront, up to $900M in milestones plus tiered royalties (total ~$1.5B) — plugging the exon-20 gap alongside AstraZeneca's osimertinib franchise and continuing the broader trend of Chinese biotech assets moving to Western majors. And a Nature Chemical Biology paper from UCL, ZSL, and Imperial College (Jervis/Tabor, published 14 July 2026) shows that common midwife toads at three recovered Pyrenean lakes survive the amphibian-killing chytrid fungus (Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis) because they deploy a rich set of antimicrobial peptides during the tadpole stage — before the fungus-vulnerable keratinized adult skin emerges — with the team cataloguing 1,152 distinct peptides where only 7 were previously known, a hidden library that could seed a new generation of human antifungals.
item.itunes:summary: Kelch13 stochastics determine artemisinin survival in resistant P. falciparum (Spielmann lab, Bernhard Nocht Institute, bioRxiv 2026-07-13): paired isogenic wild-type vs C580Y parasite lines with single-cell Kelch13 protein quantification show that low-Kelch13 parasites survive drug exposure while high-Kelch13 parasites die, mechanism via Kelch13-mediated hemoglobin endocytosis feeding heme-dependent artemisinin activation; resistance mutations shift the distribution of Kelch13 levels rather than setting a fixed phenotype; low-Kelch13 also carries a fitness cost via increased cell cycle length; implication is that partial artemisinin efficacy persists in fully mutated populations and pushing Kelch13 up could re-sensitize resistant parasites. item.title: Episode 22: The test that is making MDR-TB
item.description: A prospective cohort of 42,843 rifampin-susceptible TB patients diagnosed in Ho Chi Minh City between 2020 and 2024, with paired whole-genome sequencing of index and recurrence isolates, finds that 96% of patients who acquired rifampin resistance already carried undetected isoniazid resistance at diagnosis — a ~100-fold elevated risk — and models project that routine HR-TB diagnosis and treatment would cut new RR-TB incidence in Vietnam by 46% over 10 years, indicting the current Xpert MTB/RIF-only diagnostic paradigm as an active driver of MDR-TB. The DRC Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak reached 1,926 confirmed cases and 702 deaths as of the July 12 WHO update, +120 deaths in five days, with Ituri province accounting for 1,745 cases across 26 of 36 health zones; a companion Toronto/CIHR stochastic network modelling paper finds that improving case detection from 30% to 70% and contact tracing from 30% to 80% cuts deaths ~60% on its own, reactive ring vaccination adds only ~14% incremental benefit assuming 45% rVSV-ZEBOV cross-protection against Bundibugyo, and community vaccination at 50% coverage averts 58–86% of deaths depending on rollout delay. At AAIC 2026 in London, Eisai presented Phase 1b/2 Study 103 data on etalanetug (E2814), a monoclonal antibody targeting the microtubule-binding region of tau: plasma MTBR-tau243 fell 78% at 3 months and >90% at 9 months, CSF fell 62% and 89%, and p-tau205 dropped for the first time in dominantly inherited AD — the cleanest target-engagement package of any anti-tau antibody to date, feeding into the Tau NexGen combination trial with lecanemab. A systematic third-party audit of AlphaFold3 from the Beltrao lab at ETH Zurich tests five application areas (ubiquitinated proteins, TCR-epitope, antibody-antigen, protein-RNA, protein-lipid) and finds uneven performance driven by training-set overlap, with confidence scores failing to distinguish real from decoy RNA partners — a cautionary read for drug-discovery programs that lean heavily on AF3 for antibody and RNA tasks. And a Zoological Journal of the Linnean Society paper from a University of São Paulo team shows that harvestmen — the Opiliones arachnids, not spiders — account for more than half of all independently evolved arthropod paternal care, with 62 new records added in a two-day iNaturalist scan doubling ninety years of literature; the evolutionary mechanism appears to be sexual selection in which females prefer males already guarding eggs.
item.itunes:summary: Vietnam HR-TB → RR-TB (Spies et al., Oxford/HCMC, medRxiv 2026-07-13): 42,843-patient prospective cohort with paired WGS; 96% (49/51) of patients acquiring rifampin resistance had undetected isoniazid resistance at index; weighted risk 2.98% vs 0.03% (RR 105); modelling projects 46% reduction in RR-TB incidence over 10 years in Vietnam with universal HR-TB testing + appropriate treatment; even at 5% HR-TB prevalence, ~26% reduction — the WHO-recommended Xpert MTB/RIF diagnostic paradigm is actively generating MDR-TB. item.title: Episode 21: Why TB hits men harder
item.description: A Bishai/Klein bioRxiv preprint posted July 11 uses the Four Core Genotype mouse model (which decouples XX/XY chromosomes from gonadal sex) plus adoptive CD4+ T-cell transfer to show that female-derived CD4+ T cells confer TB protection to susceptible XY males independently of chromosome complement — via CXCR3-directed homing and CD40L-dependent organization of pulmonary B-cell follicles, with B-cell depletion revealing sex-specific failure modes (T-cell disorganization in females, exaggerated neutrophil/NET-driven inflammation in males). AstraZeneca and Ionis' Phase 3 CARDIO-TTRansform trial of eplontersen (a transthyretin antisense oligonucleotide) failed its primary composite of all-cause mortality and cardiovascular events in ATTR-CM patients over ~140 weeks: 57% of patients were on TTR stabilizers (tafamidis or acoramidis) at baseline and another 24% initiated during the trial, and eplontersen showed a 29% reduction in the primary endpoint in stabilizer-naive patients but no effect in stabilizer-treated patients — Ionis fell 21%, AstraZeneca 8%, and Alnylam's vutrisiran (Amvuttra) is now the sole TTR-knockdown drug in ATTR-CM. Goodfire and Mayo Clinic collaborators (bioRxiv, updated July 11) train a covariance probe on Evo 2 (7B-parameter genomic foundation model) that achieves 0.997 overall AUROC on 833k ClinVar SNVs and 0.991 zero-shot AUROC on 74k indels — a unified framework across missense, silent, splice, UTR, and non-coding variants — and couples it with 357 supervised annotation-disruption probes plus LLM synthesis to produce per-variant natural-language mechanistic hypotheses, available for 4.2M ClinVar variants at the EVEE web application. And Neil the Seal, a one-ton southern elephant seal (Mirounga leonina), has returned to Tasmania to undergo his annual catastrophic molt — a whole-body skin-and-fur shed elephant seals must complete on land in ~30 days — becoming a global folk hero along the way.

item.title: Episode 20: H5N1 Reaches Australia
item.description: Australia confirmed H five N one high pathogenicity avian influenza (clade 2.3.4.4b) in a greater crested tern — a locally breeding non-migratory seabird — near Robe, South Australia on 10 July 2026, bringing the national count to 13 confirmed detections in wild seabirds across three states (7 Western Australia, 5 South Australia, 1 New South Wales); arrival via transoceanic seabirds (petrels and skuas) circumvented Australia's prior protection from Asian duck flyways, and the key surveillance concern is whether the virus now reaches local duck populations and poultry. The FDA on 10 July 2026 approved enfortumab vedotin (Padcev) plus pembrolizumab (Keytruda) as perioperative treatment for all adult patients with muscle-invasive bladder cancer who are candidates for cystectomy, expanding the prior approval from cisplatin-ineligible patients only: KEYNOTE-B15 (n=808) showed 55.8% vs 32.5% pathologic complete response vs gemcitabine-cisplatin (EFS HR 0.53, OS HR 0.65), and KEYNOTE-905 (n=344) showed 57.1% vs 8.6% pCR vs immediate surgery (EFS HR 0.40, OS HR 0.50); the regimen exploits immunogenic cell death in which the Nectin-4-targeting ADC triggers tumor antigen release that is amplified by PD-1 blockade. And a new species of happy-face spider, Theridion himalayana, was described from Uttarakhand, India (above 2,000 m elevation), carrying the same red smiley-face marking as Hawaii's Theridion grallator at 8.5% genetic divergence — convergent evolution whose selective basis remains unknown, with both species sharing an unexplained parallel preference for ginger plants (Hedychium spp.).

Theridion himalayana, new spider species from the Indian Himalayas at 2,000+ m, displays the same red smiley-face marking as Hawaii's Theridion grallator at 8.5% genetic divergence — convergent evolution of an unknown-function pattern, with both species unexpectedly sharing a preference for Hedychium ginger plants.

item.title: Episode 19: Which COVID wave hit kids hardest
item.description: A retrospective cohort study of 354 SARS-CoV-2-hospitalized children at Tygerberg Hospital in Cape Town (March 2020 to June 2022) posted to medRxiv finds that pediatric COVID severity varied substantially across variants of concern, with the pre-Omicron Beta and Delta waves — not the ancestral virus or Omicron — carrying the highest burden of severe disease; younger age and admission CRP emerged as independent severity signals, underscoring the need for real-time variant surveillance in low- and middle-income settings where children already carry a heavy respiratory-disease baseline. Rhythm Pharmaceuticals' Phase 3 TRANSCEND trial of setmelanotide (MC4R agonist) in acquired hypothalamic obesity was published in NEJM: 120 patients randomized 2:1 for 52 weeks, 16.5% mean BMI reduction versus 3.3% gain on placebo (19.8% placebo-adjusted), 80% of treated patients hit ≥5% BMI drop, and clinically meaningful hunger improvement — validating the March 2026 FDA approval and demonstrating that hypothalamic-injury-driven obesity responds to restoring the MC4R signaling pathway rather than generalized appetite suppression. A University of Michigan-Kenya Ministry of Health medRxiv paper describes the DMT-PHE AI Agent: a retrieval-augmented generation agent built on Kenya's validated national public-health emergency decision framework, achieving 0.924 weighted concordance with expert gold standards across three simulated outbreak scenarios (unknown etiology, Rift Valley fever, mpox), 78.8% citation coverage with no fabricated sources, and high user trust and time-savings scores from 11 public-health professionals. OpenAI opened its GPT-5.6 family (Sol, Terra, Luna) to general availability on July 9 with a 1M-token context window, February 2026 knowledge cutoff, and API features aimed at agentic workflows; Sol scored 53.6 vs Anthropic Fable 5's 40.5 on OpenAI's Agents' Last Exam, though Fable retains a clear lead on SWE-Bench Pro (80% vs 65%). And a Journal of Fish Biology paper from the University of Hawai'i Manoa and the Minderoo-UWA Deep-Sea Research Centre documents the first-ever footage of a live goblin shark (Mitsukurina owstoni) in its natural habitat — one 2019 ROV sighting at 1,237m near Jarvis Island, and a 2024 baited-camera sighting at 1,997m on the Tonga Trench slope, the deepest confirmed observation of any mackerel shark.

item.title: Episode 18: Roche closes the Huntington's book
item.description: A preprint from the University of Alberta, Leiden, and UNC characterizes the two-pronged mechanism of CMX521, a broad-spectrum coronavirus and calicivirus nucleoside analog already through Phase 1 clinical studies: the drug stalls the SARS-CoV-2 RNA-dependent RNA polymerase briefly on incorporation, and template-embedded residues promote reverse copy-back RNA synthesis in the presence of the viral helicase, completely blocking elongation when multiple residues accumulate. Vertex Pharmaceuticals agreed to acquire Crinetics Pharmaceuticals for $10 billion -- a 102% premium and the largest deal in Vertex history -- gaining Palsonify (somatostatin receptor agonist for acromegaly, already on market) and atumelnant (CRF1-targeting agent for congenital adrenal hyperplasia, in late-stage trials), with projected combined peak sales exceeding $5 billion annually. Roche announced it is discontinuing both tominersen (antisense oligonucleotide targeting huntingtin mRNA; failed GENERATION HD2 Phase 2 on clinical functional endpoints despite hitting biomarker goals) and RG6496 (allele-selective ASO; halted in first-in-human after chronic animal dosing safety findings), ending a decade-long Huntington's disease program; UniQure's AMT-130 gene therapy is now the furthest-advanced remaining program. Absentia Labs' AI Digital Liver Model became the first artificial-intelligence drug development tool accepted into the FDA's ISTAND qualification pathway, targeting prediction of drug-induced liver injury before human trials. And a Science study led by Jay Storz at the University of Nebraska characterizes Phyllotis vaccarum, the world's highest-dwelling mammal, which survives Andean volcano summits above 6,700 m at -60 C and 44% sea-level oxygen: high-altitude populations have evolved enhanced skeletal-muscle mitochondrial respiratory capacity for thermogenesis, and both highland and lowland populations carry genes for detoxifying poisonous plant compounds.

item.title: Episode 17: The Ebola net catches Marburg
item.description: The Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in DRC has intensified to 1,708 confirmed cases and 580 deaths as of July 7, with only 32% of new confirmed cases arising from known contacts — meaning the transmission chain has largely escaped the tracing net. Enhanced surveillance built for the Ebola response in Uganda's Kyegegwa District has now caught something unexpected: a confirmed Marburg virus case in a 17-month-old child, detected because the Ebola dragnet was already looking for filovirus illness. Marburg is a close filovirus cousin of Ebola with ~50% case fatality in outbreak settings, no licensed vaccine, and a reservoir in Egyptian fruit bats. As of the latest update, contacts are being monitored and no secondary cases have been confirmed — but the source exposure remains unknown. Novartis announced it is acquiring Myricx Bio for up to US$1.5B to gain a novel antibody-drug conjugate payload class built on N-myristoyltransferase (NMT) inhibitors — a fundamentally different mechanism from the microtubule-disrupting and topoisomerase-one payloads that dominate current ADCs, with preclinical activity in topoisomerase-resistant tumor models and two lead programs targeting B7-H3 and HER2. Aureka released OpenDDE (Open Drug Discovery Engine), a 655-million-parameter all-atom co-folding model under the Apache 2.0 license, targeting the same structural-prediction niche as AlphaFold 3 but fully open for academic and commercial use, trained on ~414,000 GPU-hours and reporting competitive antibody-antigen co-folding benchmarks. OpenAI's GPT-5.6 family (Sol, Terra, Luna) — previewed to ~20 government-vetted partners for two weeks because of elevated biology and cybersecurity capability scores — opened globally today, July 9. And a University of Hawai'i team reports the first-ever footage of a living goblin shark (Mitsukurina owstoni) in its natural deep-sea habitat, extending the species' known depth range by ~700 meters and providing the first ecological observation of this 125-million-year-old lineage in the wild.

item.title: Episode 16: Bundibugyo Ebola gets its first field test
item.description: The WHO added the first-ever molecular diagnostic test for Bundibugyo virus to its Emergency Use Listing on July 2 — a Shanghai ZJ Bio-Tech RT-qPCR assay whose Bundibugyo-specific primers avoid the cross-reactivity problems of Zaire ebolavirus tests; in the days since, response-network testing capacity has grown roughly ten-fold, from 2–3 labs at 200–400 tests/day to 10 laboratories at over 2,000 tests/day, against a still-growing outbreak now at 1,561 confirmed cases and 506 deaths in the DRC (Ituri Province ~90% of cases) with Uganda having reported no new cases since June 5. AstraZeneca announced today it will pay Sino Biopharmaceutical's subsidiary Chia Tai Tianqing US$200M upfront plus up to US$1.9B in milestones and tiered double-digit royalties (~US$2.1B total) for ex-China global rights to TQC3721, an inhaled dual PDE3/4 inhibitor — same mechanism class as Merck's Ohtuvayre (ensifentrine, first-in-class, FDA-approved June 2024) — currently in Phase 3 as a nebulized suspension and Phase 2 as a dry powder inhaler formulation in China; PDE3 inhibition drives cAMP-mediated bronchodilation of airway smooth muscle, PDE4 inhibition dampens pro-inflammatory cytokines like TNF-α and IL-8, and the dry powder version is the strategic prize as it would offer a portable alternative to nebulized Ohtuvayre. A bioRxiv preprint from Brian Pierce's group at the University of Maryland systematically benchmarks AlphaFold2, AlphaFold3, increased-sampling variants, and related deep-learning methods across antibody-protein, antibody-peptide, and TCR-peptide-MHC complex modeling; AlphaFold3 and expanded sampling improve accuracy over AlphaFold2 defaults but the size of the gain varies by interface class, and pooling predictions across methods lifts near-native success for antibody-peptide complexes from 41% (best single method) to 59% — a practical prescription for antibody and vaccine design pipelines. And a Hebrew University of Jerusalem study in Ecology and Evolution (Sheizaf et al., published July 6) documents woodlice — the Middle Eastern isopod Armadillo sordidus — forming self-sustaining processions of over 5,000 individuals around the circular illuminated boundary cast by streetlights in the Golan Heights, with egg-bearing females as the majority participants; controlled trials rule out magnetic fields and UV, implicating light geometry as the trigger of an army-ant-death-spiral-like emergent behavior driven by artificial light at night.

item.title: Episode 15: Omicron's upper-airway trick, decoded
item.description: A preprint from the MRC-University of Glasgow Centre for Virus Research establishes that the H655Y spike mutation shifts SARS-CoV-2 Omicron toward cathepsin-dependent cell entry but is not the determinant of upper-airway tissue tropism — that role belongs to receptor-binding domain mutations in BA.2.86 that override H655Y entirely, mechanistically uncoupling protease preference from tissue tropism. Mpox clade Ib, after establishing local transmission in Madagascar in January 2026, accounted for 780 confirmed cases in Africa during the six-week period April 6 through May 17 — more than any other country including the DRC, whose mpox surveillance is depressed by the concurrent Bundibugyo Ebola response — and has already exported cases to Mauritius and Réunion. The FDA's PDUFA deadline for atacicept, Vera Therapeutics' dual BAFF-and-APRIL-blocking fusion protein for IgA nephropathy, falls today; the ORIGIN 3 Phase 3 trial showed 46% proteinuria reduction and the drug holds Breakthrough Therapy Designation and Priority Review status; if approved it is the first IgA nephropathy therapy to target B cell activation at the cytokine level. A City University of Hong Kong preprint describes VirProtRAG, a retrieval-augmented generation framework that annotates viral protein function by grounding predictions in retrieved scientific literature, adding non-overlapping functional annotations for roughly a third of the 17,484 Swiss-Prot viral proteins beyond existing expert curation. And fossil bee nests — named Osnidum almontei — in the tooth sockets of owl-pellet jawbones from a Hispaniola cave document the first known use of animal bones as bee nesting sites, an unintended ecological relay between owl hunting and solitary bee nest-site selection 20,000 years ago.

item.title: Episode 14: A nutritional choke point in malaria transmission
item.description: A bioRxiv preprint from Kim Williamson's group at Weill Cornell with Wageningen and Radboud collaborators identifies PfApiAT2 — one of only about a dozen membrane transporters encoded by Plasmodium falciparum — as a proline-specific transporter that is dispensable in the blood stage but essential for oocyst development in Anopheles mosquitoes; PfApiAT2-knockout parasites form stunted, degenerating oocysts and produce zero sporozoites, and the defect is fully rescued by supplementing infected mosquitoes with free amino acids, pinpointing a transmission-blocking vulnerability at the same protein that mediates resistance to the experimental antimalarial halofuginone. Novartis announced today it will acquire London-based Myricx Bio for up to US$1.5B (US$1.1B upfront plus US$400M in milestones) to add a first-in-class antibody-drug-conjugate payload class built on inhibitors of N-myristoyltransferase (NMT), an enzyme that attaches a 14-carbon myristate lipid to hundreds of human proteins that cancer cells depend on for membrane trafficking and signaling; the payload also triggers the unfolded protein response and reprograms tumor-associated macrophages, giving Novartis two lead ADC programs with a mechanism distinct from the microtubule-disrupting and DNA-damaging payloads currently dominant in the field. A bioRxiv preprint from Maha Farhat's group at Harvard with Tufts and Texas A&M collaborators systematically evaluates three active-learning strategies for whole-cell antibiotic screens, using retrospective Mycobacterium tuberculosis screening data and prospective closed-loop screening against Borrelia burgdorferi (the Lyme disease bacterium); the winning strategy — balancing predicted-hit exploitation with a novelty bonus — takes the experimental hit rate from 0.2% baseline to 1.0% (5x) and, when applied prospectively across diverse chemical space, achieves 11% confirmed activity (a 53-fold enrichment) with 100% Borrelia-selective hits. And a Matsunaga and Nose bioRxiv preprint from the University of Tokyo dissects how the elongated posterior respiratory siphon of rat-tailed maggots (Helophilus virgatus hoverfly larvae) actually deploys — not by hydraulic pressure but by a folding-unfolding mechanism driven by a dense array of ring-shaped muscle fibers that also asymmetrically bend the siphon side-to-side, revealing that the snorkel doubles as a rowing oar for near-surface locomotion.
